Legal information
Warning notice system
             This manual contains notices you have to observe in order to ensure your personal safety, as well as to prevent
             damage to property. The notices referring to your personal safety are highlighted in the manual by a safety alert
             symbol, notices referring only to property damage have no safety alert symbol. These notices shown below are
             graded according to the degree of danger.

                   DANGER
             indicates that death or severe personal injury will result if proper precautions are not taken.

                   WARNING
             indicates that death or severe personal injury may result if proper precautions are not taken.

                   CAUTION
             indicates that minor personal injury can result if proper precautions are not taken.

             NOTICE
             indicates that property damage can result if proper precautions are not taken.
             If more than one degree of danger is present, the warning notice representing the highest degree of danger will
             be used. A notice warning of injury to persons with a safety alert symbol may also include a warning relating to
             property damage.
Qualified Personnel
             The product/system described in this documentation may be operated only by personnel qualified for the specific
             task in accordance with the relevant documentation, in particular its warning notices and safety instructions.
             Qualified persons are those who, because of their training and experience, are familiar with the installation,
             assembly, commissioning, operation, decommissioning and disassembly of the product and can recognize risks
             and avoid possible hazards.
Proper use of Siemens products
             Note the following:

                   WARNING
             Siemens products may only be used for the application described in the catalog and the associated usage
             information. If products and components from other manufacturers are used, these must be recommended or
             approved by Siemens. Proper transport, storage, installation, assembly, commissioning, operation and maintenance
             are required to ensure that the products operate safely and without any problems. The permissible ambient
             conditions must be complied with. The information in the relevant documentation must be observed.

Trademarks
             All names identified by ® are registered trademarks of Siemens Aktiengesellschaft. The remaining trademarks in
             this publication may be trademarks whose use by third parties for their own purposes could violate the rights of
             the owner.
Disclaimer of Liability
             We have reviewed the contents of this publication to ensure consistency with the hardware and software
             described. Since variance cannot be precluded entirely, we cannot guarantee full consistency. However, the
             information in this publication is reviewed regularly and any necessary corrections are included in subsequent
             editions.

Introduction                                                                                                   1
1.1              About SINUMERIK
                     From simple, standardized CNC machines to premium modular machine designs – SINUMERIK
                     CNCs offer the right solution for all machine concepts. Whether for individual parts or mass
                     production, simple or complex workpieces – SINUMERIK is the highly dynamic automation
                     solution, integrated for all areas of production. From prototype construction and tool design to
                     mold making, all the way to large-scale series manufacturing.
                     Visit our website for more information SINUMERIK (https://www.siemens.com/sinumerik).




1.2              About this documentation
                     Create MyConfig engineering software supports the machine manufacturer to create and run
                     projects for automated production and commissioning of machines with SINUMERIK ONE
                     controls. Upgrades of these controls are also configured by the OEM and then performed
                     automatically at the end user.
                     The engineering software Create MyConfig comprises 4 components:
                     • CMC Diff is a comparison software that supports you in the provision of modular data.
                     • CMC Expert is a configuration software that supports you when creating a project. The
                       project is run on the control in the form of an executable package.
                     • CMC Topo is a software for configuring the topology and supports you in displaying and/or
                       generating a comparison and/or target topology for the automated commissioning of the
                       SINAMICS drive system.
                       CMC Topo is also used to support and preconfigure the axis-drive assignment.
                     • CMC Shield is the execution software, which is not installed individually. CMC Expert creates
                       an executable package that contains the software component CMC Shield, scripts,
                       instructions, and data. After starting the package, it is processed by CMC Shield according to
                       the configuration.

                     Independent tools
                     Create MyConfig also provides an autonomous tool that you can use without the engineering
                     software:
                     • DOList Editor (Page 432)
                       Editor for editing reusable and cross-topology DO lists independently of CMC Topo
                     • Resource Editor (Page 245)
                       For editing user texts in multilingual packages independently of CMC Expert.


Target group
                     This manual is intended for machine manufacturers and service technicians.

Benefits
                  As a result of the modular concept, Create MyConfig enables automatic series production and
                  the upgrade of different machines of a series with one package.
                  In contrast to conventional commissioning, individual operations on the machine are safer,
                  easier and faster to perform:
                  • The production time for machines with SINUMERIK ONE is significantly reduced.
                  • The upgrade time for end users is also reduced.
                  • A high level of reproducibility is achieved through automatic data loading.
                  • The quality of production and service is improved significantly.
                  • Less expert knowledge is required by the commissioning engineers.
                  • Modular data management for modular machines is supported at the machine
                    manufacturer's.
                  • Modular machines can adapt to flexible SINAMICS topologies.
                  • The commissioning process is documented in a log file.


Standard scope
                  This documentation only describes the functionality of the standard version. This may differ
                  from the scope of the functionality of the system that is actually supplied. Please refer to the
                  ordering documents only for the functionality of the supplied drive system.
                  It may be possible to execute other functions in the system which are not described in this
                  documentation. However, there is no obligation to supply such functions with a new control
                  or when servicing.
                  For reasons of clarity, this documentation cannot include detailed information on all product

1.2.1            Digital signature


Digital signature
                     The PDF format of this documentation is digitally signed. The digital signature ensures:
                     • Authenticity: Confirmation that the document was created by Siemens
                     • Integrity: Confirmation that content was not changed after signing


Checking the digital signature
                     • Always open the PDF document in a PDF viewer (e.g. Adobe Acrobat Reader), and not in an
                       Internet browser. Browsers either do not display digital signatures at all, or in part only.
                     • The following instructions are for the procedure in Adobe Acrobat Reader. However, the steps
                       in other PDF viewers are comparable.
                     1. Open the PDF document. The signature status is displayed at the top of the signature
                        window:
                        – Green checkmark: Signature is valid
                        – Yellow warning sign: Signature is valid, but pay attention to notes
                        – Red X: Signature is invalid or corrupted
                     2. Click on the "Signature window" button.
                     3. Expand the signature to view detailed information about the electronic signature.
                     4. You can display further details about the signature via the context menu under "Check
                        signature > Signature properties".


Solutions for invalid/corrupted signatures
                     • Download the original PDF again from the official Siemens website.
                     • Check whether the download was fully completed.
                     • Update the PDF viewer.
                     • Update the certificates.
                     • Check the system time.
                     If these approaches do not solve the problem, contact Siemens Support via SiePortal. It is
                     possible that the PDF has been manipulated by a third party.

                                                                       2.2 Create MyConfig operating environment


2.2              Create MyConfig operating environment


2.2.1            Use as prescribed


Create MyConfig
                     Create MyConfig (CMC) is used to generate commissioning packages and update packages for
                     machine tools with a SINUMERIK ONE system. This allows the automated commissioning of a
                     SINUMERIK ONE system.
                     The objective is to achieve a higher degree of automation. This enables machine builders to
                     carry out series commissioning more cost-effectively while largely eliminating human error.
                     Further, CMC is used to upgrade and update software in the field and to newly install or
                     restore CNC software.

                     Target group
                     Create MyConfig addresses trained personnel such as machine development engineers,
                     commissioning engineers and service technicians. The application either runs on Microsoft
                     Windows PCs and notebooks or in a server environment. This allows commissioning packages
                     to be automatically generated.


Engineering tools in Create MyConfig

                     Create MyConfig Expert
                     CMC Expert is the engineering software to generate a CMC project. An executable package
                     for the production or upgrading of machines is generated from the CMC project with the
                     "Create package" function. The package contains a configurable sequence of production or
                     upgrading steps and the associated data.

                     Create MyConfig Topo
                     Software CMC Topo is used in the context of Create MyConfig for:
                     Configuring, displaying, printing and comparing SINAMICS topologies

                     Create MyConfig Diff
                     CMC Diff is software for displaying and comparing:
                     • SINUMERIK archives
                     • Folders
                     • General and special data of the SINUMERIK ONE control
                     With CMC Diff, SINUMERIK archives can also be modified and stored. CMC Diff can be used to
                     support the configuration of packages with CMC Expert, and independent of CMC Expert, as
                     standard comparison software.

Safety instructions
2.2 Create MyConfig operating environment


                      Create MyConfig DOList Editor
                      To edit a DO list independent of CMC Expert and CMC Topo, use the "Create MyConfig DOList
                      Editor". The DOList Editor with MCL editor is used to create a global DO variables list, e.g.
                      for a machine series, including the creation of a predefined axis-drive assignment and the
                      machine concept list. The result is used in the EPLAN add-in or in the engineering & service
                      workflow for automated axis-drive assignment.

                      Create MyConfig Resource Editor
                      CMC supports the use of language resources without their management. Language resources
                      can be edited using the CMC resource editor.

                      Create MyConfig – EPLAN Electric P8 Add-In
                      With the add-in, EPLAN topologies, components and their assignments can be automatically
                      transferred into a Create MyConfig project. There, they can be used to configure machines
                      and generate topologies.


Runtime environment

                      Create MyConfig Shield
                      CMC Shield is the execution software that is not individually installed. CMC Expert generates
                      an executable package with the following content:
                      • CMC Shield software components
                      • Scripts
                      • Instructions and data
                      By starting the package, CMC Shield processes the package according to the configuration.




2.2.2           Intended operating environment and security assumptions from the risk
                analysis
                      The individual components of Create MyConfig have different applications. As a consequence,
                      the intended operating environments differ. Depending on the criticality of the data, which are
                      processed within the scope of this tool, additional requirements arise relating to the security of
                      the usage environment.


Generating CMC packages
                      Create MyConfig applications are classic engineering tools. These are used to generate packages
                      for series commissioning or for updates. As a consequence, the intended operating
                      environment is an office PC or laptop in the development department of a machine builder.
                      Operation is carried out by authorized and trained personnel who can assess the criticality of the
                      data used and store and use it accordingly.
                      Secure use of the product requires a properly maintained IT environment (up-to-date
                      operating system, antivirus protection and individualized user access).

                                                                        2.2 Create MyConfig operating environment


                     The data used are managed within the framework of criticality in a standard IT environment
                     of a customer.

                     Example for an accepted target environment
                     The PC or laptop of the employee in the office is protected in accordance with company
                     directives (updated operating system, antivirus protection etc. individualized access etc.).
                     Archiving data either on the employee's computer or at a storage location managed by the
                     company (e.g. Cloud, network drives, SharePoint etc.)


Adding security-relevant data
                     To handle security-relevant data in plain text until it is encrypted by Create MyConfig Expert, a
                     high-security environment is assumed, such as a server with restricted access.

                     Example for an accepted target environment
                     A server with appropriate physical and logical safeguards, as well as authorization
                     mechanisms and access restrictions corresponding to the required level of protection.


Transferring CMC packages
                     Using Create MyConfig Expert, at the end, an executable package is generated with which a
                     machine tool can be equipped and configured with a software release. As a consequence, the
                     integrity and confidentiality of CMC packages are of primary importance. It is assumed that
                     confidentiality, integrity and authenticity are ensured by the respective transmission channel
                     (e.g. encrypted/signed email, data exchange server, etc.). Also in this case, it is assumed that
                     trained and authorized personnel are involved, who are conscious of the criticality of the data
                     and use this data appropriately.




2.2.3            Foreseeable incorrect use
                     The use of Create MyConfig in a way not intended by the manufacturer, but which may occur due
                     to typical, foreseeable human behavior.


Examples

                     IT environment of the machine OEM not appropriately protected
                     This can lead to unauthorized access to data, possibly also security-relevant data so that
                     access data or know-how of the OEM are compromised. When an attacker manipulates the
                     data, then the data integrity can be at risk.

                     Archiving security-relevant data in areas that are either not protected or inadequately
                     protected
                     This can lead to unauthorized access to security-relevant data (e.g. passwords) so that access
                     data or know-how of the OEM are compromised.

                      is in transit or stored. This could result in access data or know-how of the OEM being

4.1              Overview
                     You have 2 options for installing engineering software "Create MyConfig" on your PC:
                     • Installation using the installation wizard
                       The CMC package is installed using the General setup.
                       The General setup involves the installation of Create MyConfig and the Application License
                       Managers (ALM).
                       More information can be found in the following sections:
                        – User-guided setup (Page 31)
                        – Performing the automated installation (Page 31)
                     • Installation via command line
                       It can also be automatically installed without any user interaction.


                     Note
                     • You can install and use CMC V6.10 in parallel with previous versions CMC 4.5, 4.6 HF1,
                       4.7 SP2 HF1, CMC 4.8 SP1 and V6.2 to V6.9.
                     • For a user-prompted setup, CMC V6.10 components can also be individually installed.




License
                     Create MyConfig can only be used with a valid license. The license is managed by the Automation
                     License Manager (ALM). The Automation License Manager is installed automatically while
                     setting up Create MyConfig.
                     The license is queried:
                     • When starting CMC Expert
                     • When starting CMC Diff
                     • When starting CMC Topo
                     • For a command line call of the 3 programs listed
                     A 30 day test license is installed with Create MyConfig. The 30 day runtime is activated when
                     the program is called for the first time.

4.2            Information regarding compatibility

Compatibility between SINUMERIK versions and CMC versions
                  • As of SINUMERIK V6.23, the use of Create MyConfig V6.6 or lower is not supported.
                  • Create MyConfig V6.10 conditionally supports SINUMERIK versions lower than V6.23.
                  • The following functions introduced with Create MyConfig V6.8 SP1 can only be used together
                    with SINUMERIK V6.24 or higher:
                     – Configuring the security archive password.
                     – PLC start interlock is set while the package is being executed.
                  • The following functions introduced with Create MyConfig V6.10 can only be used together
                    with SINUMERIK from V6.25 SP1 and higher:
                     – Logging in at the NCU with UMC access data




4.3            Hardware requirements
                  A PC/PG must meet the following requirements for the installation and operation of Create
                  MyConfig (CMC):
                  • The drive on which the software is to be installed has approx. 900 MB of free memory.
                  • Additional memory is required to create your own projects.
                  • All graphics-capable printers supported by the operating system can be used.
                  • A USB data storage medium with or without Linux boot system (USB flash drive, USB hard
                    disk, etc.) or a network connection is required to perform a new installation of the NCU.
                  • For a new installation, take into account the preconditions described in the release notes for
                    the particular SINUMERIK version.

6.3            Locations where the script language is used


Locations where the script languages is used
                   The section "Create MyConfig - CMC script" describes a simple programming language that is
                   based on known elements of other programming languages.
                   You can create scripts for dialogs and steps, action scripts for actions of the type "Copy",
                   "Change INI", "Create with preprocessor", "Delete", "Execute", and for CMC Diff.
                   The "Script Editor" integrated in CMC Expert supports you when creating and editing scripts
                   by:
                   • Syntax highlighting
                   • Extensive shortcut menu

                   You use scripts in:
                   • Dialogs ("dialog scripts (Page 258)")
                   • Steps (CMC Expert > Steps (Page 338))
                   • Actions (CMC Expert > Actions > "Action scripts (Page 353)")
                   • Change orders: Examples of an action script (CMC Expert > Actions > "Change INI
                     (Page 360)" / "Create with preprocessor (Page 362)")
                   • CMC Diff ("CMC scripts in CMC Diff (Page 170)")


Dialogs
                   You can have scripts executed at fixed times on almost all dialog pages.
                   You can find more information under "Dialog scripts (Page 258)".


Steps
                   You can save scripts for each step, which are executed when executing the step.
                   Using scripts, you can control the current step and all subsequent steps.

6.4.2               Using system variables


6.4.2.1             Up.$Env.BatchMode
                      Command line execution of CMC scripts in CMC Diff is always realized in the "Batch mode".
                      Using system variable Up.$Env.BatchMode, you can interrogate as to whether the CMC
                      script is in the "Batch mode", i.e. the CMC script was started via the command line.


Example
                      If you do not wish to call any dialogs while running the script in the "Batch mode", then make the
                      call dependent on the dialog of variables Up.$Env.BatchMode.

                      If Up.$Env.BatchMode == false
                       Msg("The CMC script was started from the user interface of CMC
                       Diff.")
                      EndIf


6.4.2.2             Up.$Script.ScriptFile
                      Variable Up.$Script.ScriptFile contains the absolute path of the script file that is
                      executed.
                      Using this variable, you check whether the correct CMC script was started.


Example

                      If Up.$Script.ScriptFile != "P:\Manufact\Diff_Script\myscript.upscr"
                       Error("The incorrect CMC script was started! It is possible that
                       this CMC script is not current!")
                      EndIf

                                                                                         Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                        6.4 System variables - CMC scripts in CMC Diff



                     Note
                     Case sensitivity of paths
                     It is important that you take into account the case sensitivity if you perform a string comparison
                     of paths. Under Microsoft Windows, this is not relevant in the file system.
                     When comparing string values in the CMC script you must take into account the case sensitivity.




6.4.2.3          Up.$Script.ArcFile
                     For command line execution, the system variable contains the absolute path of the result
                     archive, which was specified using the command line switch /outarc.
                     When starting the CMC script via the user interface, the variable contains the absolute path
                     of the (result) archive on which the CMC script is applied.


Example
                     MSG("The archive '$(Up.$Script.ArcFile)' is manipulated by the CMC
                     script.")


6.4.2.4          Up.$Script.Result
                     You require this system variable for data export of your CMC script in CMC Diff. All files that you
                     assign to these system variables in the CMC script are transferred from CMC Diff to the instance
                     that calls the script.
                     When starting the CMC script from the user interface of the CMC Diff, after the script has
                     been run, then the files are opened and transferred to the user. The user saves the files with
                     "Save as" in the linked standard application at the required location.
                     When starting the CMC script from the command line, after the script has been executed, the
                     files are saved or transferred corresponding to the argument of switch /result.
                     You only require system variable Up.$Script.Result if these two conditions are satisfied:
                     • When using procedures that generate files,
                       File operations, e.g. TraceToFile()
                     • When using relative paths in these procedures,
                       e.g. because the CMC script is to run on various configured computers


Example 1 - exporting a file

                     Content CMC script "myScript.upscr":

                     TraceToFile(".\myTrace.txt", "my trace output")
                     Up.$Script.Result = ".\myTrace.txt"




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                           41
Create MyConfig - CMC script
6.4 System variables - CMC scripts in CMC Diff


                   Content batch script (CMD) for command line:

                   @echo off
                   echo script is running ...
                   set cmc_diff="C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create
                   MyConfig 6.10\Diff.exe"
                   set script="myScript.upscr"
                   set arc_file="mync.dsf"
                   set out_arc="mync_new.dsf"
                   set script_log="myScript.html"
                   set result="C:\Temp\myResult.txt"

                   %cmc_diff% /script %skript% /inarc %arc_file% /outarc %out_arc% /
                   result %result% /scriptlog %script_log% /log cmdLog.xml
                   echo Errorlevel is: %Errorlevel%
                   Pause

                   Result after executing the batch and CMC script:
                   After executing the CMC script using the command line call, the content of file "myTrace.txt"
                   is located in file "C:\Temp\myResult.txt".
                   After executing the CMC script when started at the CMC Diff user interface, the content of
                   file "myTrace.txt" is in the editor. You save the file using "Save as" at a location that you can
                   arbitrarily select.


Example 2 - exporting several files
                   When exporting several files, use a semicolon to separate the files. Assign the files as string
                   variable to system variable Up.$Script.Result.
                   The path of a folder is saved in the batch script for the argument of switch /result. The
                   exported files are saved in this folder.

                   Content CMC script "myScript.upscr":

                   TraceToFile(".\myTrace.txt", "my trace output")
                   FileCopy(ARC, "NC/initial.ini", RTS, ".\initial.ini")
                   Up.$Script.Result = ".\TraceToFile.txt;.\initial.ini"
                   Alternatively, you can also assign the files using package variables and concatenate operator
                   or using package variables and replacement operator.

                   Using package variables and concatenate operator:

                   Up.File1 = ".\myTrace.txt"
                   Up.File2 = ".\initial.ini"
                   Up.$Script.Result = Up.File1 << ";" << Up.File2

                                                                                       Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                      6.4 System variables - CMC scripts in CMC Diff


                     Using package variables and replacement operator:

                     Up.$Script.Result = "$(Up.File1) ; $(Up.File2)"

                     Content batch script (CMD) for command line:

                     @echo off
                     echo script is running ...
                     set cmc_diff="C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create
                     MyConfig 6.10\Diff.exe"

                     "initial.ini" are located in the folder "C:\Temp\myResult". If the folder does not
                     exist, then CMC Diff automatically creates the folder.
                     After running the CMC script via Start on CMC Diff interface, the files "myTrace.txt"
                     and "initial.ini" are each opened in an editor. You save the files using "Save as" at a
                     location that you can arbitrarily select.

6.5 Script libraries



                       Note
                       Starting the CMC script via the command line
                       When starting a CMC script via the command line, CMC Diff is always automatically in the Edit
                       mode. For command line execution, system variable UP.$Script.EditMode always has the
                       value true.




6.5              Script libraries
                       Frequently used script blocks can be stored in libraries as procedures or functions so that these
                       script blocks are available for several projects or CMC scripts in CMC Diff.


Notes in CMC scripts in CMC Diff

                       Note
                       Using script libraries in CMC scripts in CMC Diff
                       You have the following options to publish your own libraries if you want to use your own
                       functions and procedures from your script libraries in CMC:
                       • Store your libraries next to the CMC script for CMC Diff. In this way, all scripts are in the same
                          folder.
                       • Store the libraries in a path (folder) of the environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH%.
                       • Include your archive path in the variable.
                       Environment variable %UP_LIB_PATH% is only relevant when executing CMC scripts in
                       CMC Diff.

                       Note
                       Identifying script libraries
                       When starting a CMC script in CMC Diff via the user interface or a command line call, the script
                       libraries are read-in one after the other in the following sequence:
                       • Libraries next to the script
                       • 1st path in %UP_LIB_PATH%
                       • 2nd path in %UP_LIB_PATH%
                       • ...
                       • n. path in %UP_LIB_PATH%
                       If the definition of a procedure or function is available in more than one script library (multiple
                       definition of the same function or procedure), a corresponding error message is generated when
                       the CMC script is manually started using the CMC Diff user interface. You then have the option
                       of continuing or cancelling.
                       When the CMC script is started via the command line, the error message is written to the
                       logbook. CMC Shield uses the first definition found in accordance with the search sequence
                       described above.

                                                                                    6.6 CMC standard script libraries


6.6              CMC standard script libraries
                     The CMC standard script libraries are provided by Create MyConfig:
                     • SINAMICS (Page 45)
                     • Utilities (Page 46)
                     You can find standard script libraries under the following path:
                     • C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create MyConfig 6.10\UpLib




6.6.1            SINAMICS


6.6.1.1          SINAMICS library


Function/procedure of the "SINAMICS" library
                     The SinamicsTecActivate() and the SinamicsTecDeactivate() procedures are
                     available in the "SINAMICS“ library. The procedures activate or deactivate technological
                     functions in the drive.


6.6.1.2          SinamicsTecActivate


SinamicsTecActivate("<TECNAME>", <DoVar>)
                     The SinamicsTecActivate() procedure activates technological functions of the drive.
                     The technological functions must be available on the SD card at the start of the CMC
                     package. You can also install the technological functions via "Additional software (*tgz)"
                     in the same package.
                     The procedure ensures that the corresponding index of the r4956[x] parameter is set in the
                     servo or the r4993[x] parameter in the CU.
                     The <TECNAME> argument must contain the name of the technological function, in
                     accordance with parameter p4955[x] (OA DO-specific Indentifier).
                     The <DoVar> argument contains the path of the DO to inform the procedure in which drive
                     object the technological function must be activated.
                     The specific user parameters of the technological functions must be set independently
                     through scripts.
                     In principle, this function can be called in all:
                     • Dialog scripts
                     • Action scripts
                     • Scripts
                     • CMC scripts in CMC Diff



Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                        45
Create MyConfig - CMC script
6.6 CMC standard script libraries


Examples

                   Example 1
                   Activate the "Trace buffer" function in the CU Integrated with absolute addressing.
                   SinamicsTecActivate("TRCBUF", B3_S13_PS1)

                   Example 2
                   Activate the "Servo Coupling" function in a servo with variable addressing.
                   SinamicsTecActivate("SERVCOUP", Up.AXSP1M_00)


6.6.1.3         SinamicsTecDeactivate


SinamicsTecDeactivate(“<TECNAME>“, <DoVar>)
                   The SinamicsTecDeactivate() procedure deactivates technological functions of the drive.
                   This procedures functions in the same way as the SinamicsTecActivate() procedure,
                   but with deactivation of the technological functions.




6.6.2           Utilities


6.6.2.1         Utilities library


Functions of the "Utilities" library
                   The IsBit(), SetBit() and ClrBit() functions are available in the "Utilities" library. You
                   can manipulate or query the individual bits of any variables with these functions.


6.6.2.2         IsBit


IsBit(<bit>,<value>)
                   The IsBit() function determines whether a bit is set. When the specified bit is set, the function
                   returns the value "true" or "false".
                   In principle, the IsBit() function called is possible in all:
                   • Dialog scripts
                   • Action scripts
                   • Scripts
                   • CMC scripts in CMC Diff
                   You specify which bit is to be queried via the <bit> argument. The bits of a value are
                   counted from right to left starting with bit "0".


                                                                                        Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
46                                                                           Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                      Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                                  6.6 CMC standard script libraries


                     The <value> argument designates the identifier in whose value a bit is queried.
                     Identifiers are, for example:
                     • Up variables
                     • Machine data
                     • NC data
                     • Drive data
                     • Display data


Example
                     Up.bit_is = isBit(20,$MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0])


6.6.2.3          SetBit


SetBit(<bit>,<value>)
                     The SetBit() function sets a bit to the value "1".
                     In principle, this function can be called in all:
                     • Dialog scripts
                     • Action scripts
                     • Scripts
                     • CMC scripts in CMC Diff
                     You specify which bit is to be queried via the <bit> argument. The bits of a value are
                     counted from right to left starting with bit "0".
                     The <value> argument designates the identifier in whose value a bit is to be set.
                     Identifiers are, for example:
                     • Up variables
                     • Machine data
                     • NC data
                     • Drive data
                     • Display data


Example
                     $MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0] = SetBit(4,$MN_USER_DATA_HEX[0])

6.6.2.4        ClrBit


ClrBit(<bit>,<value>)
                  The ClrBit() function resets a bit to the value "0".
                  In principle, this function can be called in all:
                  • Dialog scripts
                  • Action scripts
                  • Scripts
                  • CMC scripts in CMC Diff
                  You specify which bit is to be reset via the <bit> argument. The bits of a value are counted
                  from right to left starting with bit "0".
                  The <value> argument designates the identifier in whose value a bit is to be reset.

                  • Up variables
                  • Machine data
                  • NC data
                  • Drive data
                  • Display data

6.8                 Package variables


Package variables - Up.<identifier>
                      Package variables are variables that have significance only within a package. The control does
                      not recognize package variables. Therefore, package variables are not transferred to the
                      controller.
                      The package variables comprise an identifier, preceded by the "Up." prefix.
                      The characters that are also permissible in the NC for <identifier> are permissible for the
                      identifier. In principle, the same rules therefore apply as with the NC, e.g. no umlauts, no
                      spaces.

                      Depending on their definition, package variables are classified according to the
                      following categories:

Category                Defined by                                         Value allocation by
Script                  User texts in scripts                              User


DO (drive object)       User in "SINAMICS topology" dialog page or via     System
                        the DOVar function


System                  The system using the package configuration         System

Variable                Syntax *                                           Description
Script variable         Up.<Name>                                          Value of an Up variable


DO variable             Up.<Name>.<Property>                               Property value of a DO variable (drive variable)


System variable         Up.$<SysName>.<Property>                           Property value of a system variable


* Package variables are identified by the "Up." prefix.

                     underscore and comprises the characters A-Z_0-9. Uppercase/lowercase is not relevant.
                     Package variables that receive their value from the system can only be accessed in read-only
                     mode.

6.8.3            System variables

6.9              Functions and procedures


Comparison of functions and procedures
                     Functions and procedures are subprograms, which are called up together with parameters. The
                     parameters are transferred in the form of arguments.
                     The difference between functions and procedures is that procedures do not supply a direct
                     return value.
                     Functions supply one direct return value, e.g. a value that the operator entered.

                     You can only use functions at the following locations:
                     • Within comparisons
                     • As argument of other functions or procedures
                     • To the right of a "="

                     Special issue relating to procedures:
                     Procedures must be located alone in one line.

                     You can use the following as arguments for functions and procedures:
                     • Constant value
                     • Variable
                     • Up variables
                     • System variables

                  Double inverted commas
                  If user interface text contains a function in double inverted commas ", change the double

                  the case in the NC.

                  Incorrect formatting
                  If an error occurs when formatting texts, this can lead to the entire formatting of the logbook
                  being changed or corrupted starting at this error. This is the case, for example, if a tag is not
                  closed or is written incorrectly.

6.12 Control structures


                   Control structures used in CMC
                   The following variants of the control structures are available:
                   • If control structure (Page 62)
                   • If-Else control structure (Page 62)
                   • If-ElsIf control structure (Page 62)
                   • If-ElsIf-Else control structure (Page 62)
                   • While control structure (Page 64)
                   Display and use only in the preprocessor script:
                   • #Pragma Eol control structure (Page 64)
                   • #Rem control structure (Page 65)




6.12.2          If control structure / If-Else control structure


Conditional execution - If ... Else ... EndIf

                                If exp
                                    block1
                                Else
                                    block2
                                EndIf

                   The control structure allows the conditional execution of two different instruction blocks
                   depending on whether the "exp" condition is fulfilled or not. If it is fulfilled (true), then the
                   first operation block "block1" is executed, else the second execution "block2" is executed.
                   Each of the two instruction blocks can, in turn, contain control structures; this means that
                   any nesting depth is possible.

                   Example
                                CHANDATA(1)
                                If Up.Velo_X != null
                                  If Up.Velo_X > ($MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1]+ 100)
                                    $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = Up.Velo_X
                                  Else
                                    $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = 1000
                                  EndIf
                                EndIf




6.12.3          If-ElsIf control structure / If-ElsIf-Else control structure
                   After the If condition alternative conditions can be checked by specifying ElsIf or ElIf.
                   The instruction block is executed after the first fulfilled condition. The instruction block after
                   Else is executed if no condition is fulfilled.




                                                                                         Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
62                                                                            Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                          Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                                                 6.12 Control structures


                     Conditional execution - If ... ElsIf... Else... EndIf

                                  If exp
                                    block_1
                                  ElsIf exp_2
                                    block_2
                                  ElsIf exp_3
                                    block_3
                                  …
                                  Else
                                    block_E
                                  EndIf


                     Note
                     For the alternative conditions, the keywords "ElsIf" and "ElIf" are used as equivalents.


                     The control structure allows the conditional execution of different instruction blocks
                     depending on whether the "exp" condition is fulfilled or not.
                     If this is fulfilled (true), then the 1st instruction block "block_1" is executed. Otherwise, it is
                     checked whether the next alternative condition "exp_2" is fulfilled or not.
                     If this is fulfilled (true), then the 2nd instruction block "block_2" is executed. Otherwise, it is
                     checked whether the next alternative condition "exp_3" is fulfilled or not.
                     If this is fulfilled (true), then the third instruction block "block_3" is executed, and so on.
                     As soon as a condition or alternative condition is fulfilled, the associated instruction block is
                     executed. Execution continues after the associated keyword "EndIf".
                     As long as the condition or alternative condition is not fulfilled, the subsequent alternative
                     condition is checked.
                     If no alternative condition is fulfilled, the instruction block "block_E" in the alternative
                     branch is executed after the keyword "Else".
                     If no alternative branch "Else" was specified, then processing is continued after the keyword
                     "EndIf" without executing an instruction block.
                     Each instruction block can, in turn, contain control structures. Any nesting depth is possible.

                     Example 1
                                  CHANDATA(1)
                                  If Up.Velo_X != null
                                    If Up.Velo_X > $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1]
                                      $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = Up.Velo_X
                                    Else
                                      $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1] = 1000
                                    EndIf
                                  EndIf

Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                               63
Create MyConfig - CMC script
6.12 Control structures



                   Example 2 - Alternative condition
                               IF (up.selection == 1)
                                Log("selection 1")
                               ELSIF (up.selection == 2)
                                Log("selection 2")
                               ELIF (up.selection == 3)
                                Log("selection 3")
                               ELSE
                                Log("selection was not 1, 2 or 3")
                               ENDIF




6.12.4          While control structure


Repeated execution - While ... EndWhile

                               While exp
                                    block
                               EndWhile

                   The control structure allows the repeated execution of the operation block "block" as long as
                   the "exp" condition is fulfilled.
                   The operation block can, in turn, contain control structures; this means that any nesting
                   depth is possible.

                   Example
                               [B3_S3_PS99]
                               Up.i = 0
                               Up.CU_Hat_Servo = false
                               While Up.i < 6 && !Up.CU_Hat_Servo
                                 If p978[$(Up.i)] != 255
                                   Up.CU_Hat_Servo = true
                                 EndIf
                                 Up.i += 1
                               EndWhile

6.13             Operators


6.13.1           Assignment operators


Assignment operators - VAR = 123
                     The assignment operators constitute the core function of scripts, as they write the control data.
                     All assignment operators can also be applied to script variables.

                     Table 6-7         The following assignment operators are available:

                      ?=         Assign if blank or not available
                                 Assign the specified value if no value is available.
                                 No assignment is made if a value is already available.


                      =          Assign
                                 Assignment of a new value.
                                 The assignment is always executed. If the data item or variable does not yet exist, then it is
                                 created.
                                 If the data item or variable already exists, then the value is changed.
                                 An assignment of "null" deletes the variables or resets the value to the default value.


                      ∼          Delete
                                 The data and the value are removed.
                                 For control data (NC/drive data), this generally means that the value is reset to the default value
                                 of the control (of the software release).


                      +=         Add
                                 Addition of the specified value to the existing value.


                      -=         Subtract
                                 Subtraction of the specified value from the existing value


                      *=         Multiply
                                 Multiplication of the specified value and the existing value.




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                                        65
Create MyConfig - CMC script
6.13 Operators


                    /=         Divide
                               Division of the existing value by the specified value.


                    |=         OR operation
                               OR operation on the specified and existing value (set bits).


                    &=         AND operation
                               AND operation on the specified and existing value (reset bits).


                    :=         Assignment without evaluation
                               Assignment without evaluation to the right of the operator. The value is transferred to the
                               control as specified.
                               Everything to the right of "=" (e.g. a variable) is neither interpreted by the package nor processed.


                   An error message is output if a value does not exist for compounded operators "+= -=
                   *= /= &= |=".

                   Examples
                                   N20000 $MC_CHAN_NAME="TUTORIAL"
                                   $ON_AXIS_FUNCTION_MASK~
                                   $MA_AX_VELO_LIMIT[0,AX1]?=2300
                                   R[0]+=10
                                   $MN_MM_TOOL_MANAGEMENT_MASK|='B10000'
                                   GUD_2=$MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX1]
                                   Up.myVar ~ ; Delete variable
                                   Up.myVar = null ; Delete variable (alternative)

6.13.4           Special operators


Replacement operator - $(up.?)
                   The "replacement operator" makes it is possible to replace parts of an instruction, an identifier,
                   a value or a message text flexibly with the value of a package variable "Up.identifier".

                   Note the following rules when applying the "replacement operator":
                   • Use only with package variables.
                     More information is provided in the section "Package variables (Page 52)".
                   • During replacement, straight quotation marks are removed from string values.
                   • "Replacement operators" can be nested.

                   Examples for applying the "replacement operator":
                   • In sections
                     [$(up.doX.pspath)] or [B3_S$(Up.slave)_PS$(Up.doNr)]
                   • In identifiers
                     $MA_MAX_AX_VELO[AX$(UP.AXNr)]=1000
                   • In parameter indices
                     If p107[$(Up.i)] == 254
                   • In comparison operations
                     Version(PCU, "SINUMERIK ONE Operate")>=$(Up.HMI)
                   • In functions and procedures
                     MSG("Maschinennummer: $(Up.Masch_Nr)")

6.14.3           StringPos


StringPos("<string>", "<search>", <pos>)
                     The StringPos() function searches in the <string> character string for the <search>
                     character string, starting at the <pos> position.
                     In principle, this function can be called in all "Dialog scripts", "Action scripts", scripts and
                     "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                     The <search> character string to be sought is specified via a regular expression. The case-
                     sensitivity in the <search> argument is not relevant and is not observed.
                     The function returns the position of the first occurrence of <search> as decimal number. If
                     the <search> character string was not found, a -1 is returned.
                     When assessing the returned positions, note that the first character in the <string> is on
                     the 0 position. Spaces in the <string> are also characters, non-printable characters.

                     Note
                     Using metacharacters as character literals
                     Take special care when using metacharacters as character literals in a regular expression.
                     More information on regular expressions is available under Create MyConfig - Diff, in Section
                     "Use of regular expressions in CMC Diff (Page 214)".




Example

                     Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "e", 0)                               ;Up.Pos = 3
                     Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "E", 5)                               ;Up.Pos = 17
                     Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "e", 25)                              ;Up.Pos = -1
                     Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "x", 0)                               ;Up.Pos = -1
                     Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "for", 0)                             ;Up.Pos = 10
                     Up.Pos=StringPos("Ingenuity for life", "[efg]", 0)                           ;Up.Pos = 2




6.14.4           StringReplace


StringReplace("<string>", "<search>", "<replace>")
                     The StringReplace() function searches in the <string> character string for the <search>
                     character string and replaces it with the <replace> character string.
                     In principle, this function can be called in all "Dialog scripts", "Action scripts", scripts and
                     "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                     The return value of the function is a character string with the replaced characters.
                     The <search> character string to be sought is specified via a regular expression.

                   The case-sensitivity in the <search> argument is relevant and is observed. Replacement
                   is made only when identical. If nothing to be replaced is found, the function returns the
                   <string> argument unchanged.
                   Multiple occurrences of the sought <search> characters are all replaced.

                   Note
                   Using metacharacters as character literals

6.15             File operations
                     The functions and procedures that you can use for files are described in the following sections.

                     In the subsequent sections, the following values are uniformly permissible for
                     argument <area>:
                     • RTS
                        – For the runtime system (NCU, PC/IPC) on which the package is executed
                        – You can specify the path, either in relative terms, starting next to the package, or in
                          absolute terms
                        – The use of environment variables is possible
                     • ARC
                        – For the archive folder, i.e. the image of the SINUMERIK archive
                        – You specify the path in relative terms, starting with NC, DRV, HMI or SYS
                     • NCU
                        – For the file system of the NCU
                        – You specify the path in absolute terms, starting with "/" and taking into account uppercase/
                          lowercase (case sensitive)
                     • PCU
                        – For the file system of the PCU
                        – You specify the path in absolute terms, starting with the drive letter, e.g. "D:\" or "D$\"


                     Note
                     Activating data areas
                     You only reach the areas that you have activated in CMC Expert in the "Project explorer" in the
                     "Configuration (Page 237)" under the "Data areas" property group.

6.15.1          FileCopy


FileCopy(<area>, "<sourcepath>", <area>, "<destinationpath>")
                   The FileCopy() procedure copies a file from a source to a target across areas.
                   In principle, this procedure can be called in all scripts, "dialog scripts", "action scripts" and
                   "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                   The areas for the source and target are specified via the <area> argument.
                   The permissible values for the <area> argument are provided in Section "File operations
                   (Page 73)".
                   The <sourcepath> argument specifies the source path of the file to be copied.
                   The <destinationpath> argument specifies the target path of the file.

                   already exists in the target, it will be overwritten without a prompt.
                   If the package runs on the NCU, copying to the PCU via <area> PCU is not possible.

                   Up.cf = "./CF-" << Up.$Env.SDID << "/"

                   (Up.cf)hwversions.xml")
                   FileCopy(NCU, "/siemens/versions.xml", RTS, "$
                   (Up.cf)siemens_versions.xml")

                     FileWrite(RTS,"$(Up.$Pack.Dir)/MyText.txt", Up.myfile) ;path specification
                     via system variable.

                     Note
                     Use of the end of line / line break
                     If your character string has several lines, you can implement it with the string concatenation
                     operator.
                     You can find more information in Section "String concatenation operator (Page 69)".
                     Example
                     FileWrite(RTS,"MyText.txt","Line 1"<<'\r'<<'\n'<<"Line
                     2"<<'\r'<<'\n')
                     \r → Carriage return (CR or 0x0D)
                     \n → Line feed (LF or 0x0A)

                     Note
                     Attaching characters to an existing file
                     If you attach characters to an existing file, you can implement this in two ways:
                     1. Use the TraceToFile() procedure. This procedure has the advantage that it always has
                         high performance.
                         Only use TraceToFile() for the runtime system (RTS). First copy the file to the runtime
                         system, attach the file and then copy back the file.
                         This procedure can be used when you write several times to the file and only copy the file back
                         after all the write operations.
                         You can find more information in Section "TraceToFile (Page 84)".
                         Example
                         ;If the package is executed on the PG/PC
                         FileCopy(PCU, "D:\LastUpdate.txt", RTS, "LastUpdate.txt")
                         TraceToFile("LastUpdate.txt", "Step 4711 successful")
                         ...
                         FileCopy(RTS, "LastUpdate.txt", PCU, "D:\LastUpdate.txt")
                     2. Read the contents of a file with the FileRead() procedure.
                         Add your characters with the string concatenation operator (Concate-Operator) "<<" and
                         write the STRING back to the file with FileWrite().
                         Example
                         FileWrite(RTS, "RW.txt",FileRead(RTS,"RW.txt")<<'\r'<<'\n'<< "my
                         attached line")




6.15.6           QueryIni


QueryIni("<path>", "<section/id>")
                     The QueryIni() function reads values from INI files.




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                           79
Create MyConfig - CMC script
6.15 File operations


                   In principle, this function can be called in all "Dialog scripts", "Action scripts", scripts and
                   "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                   You can use this function for all files whose structure corresponds to the format of an INI file
                   and are located on the runtime system (RTS) of the package execution.

                   These files have the following structure:
                   [Section]
                   Identifier = value
                   Using the <path> argument, you specify the file (with path and file name) from where a
                   value is read.
                   You can specify the file path fully qualified in accordance with the runtime system - or also
                   relative to the package.
                   Using <section/id>, you specify the section and the identifier for the value to be read.
                   <section/id> is not case sensitive.
                   Exception: <path> on the NCU (Linux) is case sensitive.
                   The return value of the function is the value of the specified identifier in the section of the
                   file.
                   The function returns "null" if the specified file, the section or the Identifier is not found. Or, if
                   there is no equal character and no value at the identifier.
                   If there is an equals sign, but no value at the queried Identifier, the function returns an empty
                   string "".
                   You can use the environment system variables of the runtime system.
                   By testing the return value for "null", you can determine whether or not the function could
                   find the file, the section or the identifier.


Example 1
                   Query the "FirewallOpenPorts" identifier in the "LinuxBase" section in
                   the "basesys.ini" file.

                   Content of "basesys.ini"

                   [LinuxBase]
                   FirewallOpenPorts="TCP/5900 TCP/102 TCP/22"

                   Function call in CMC Expert

                   Up.FOP = QueryIni("/user/system/etc/basesys.ini","LinuxBase/
                   FirewallOpenPorts")
                   MSG("The FirewallOpenPorts are:$(Up.FOP)")

                   Function return value
                   Up.FOP contains the function return value: e.g. "TCP/5900 TCP/102 TCP/22".

6.15.7           QueryXml


QueryXml("<path>", "<xpath>")
                     The QueryXml() function reads the contents of XML files that are on the runtime system (RTS)
                     of the package execution.
                     In principle, this function can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts, "action scripts" and "CMC
                     scripts in CMC Diff".
                     The <path> argument specifies the XML file with path and file names (file path) from where
                     the content of an XML node should be read. Whereby, the file path can be specified fully
                     qualified, in accordance with the runtime system, or also relative to the package.
                     For Linux (NCU), the case sensitivity of the path is relevant, but not for Microsoft Windows
                     (PC/IPC ).
                     The XPath expression in the <xpath> argument selects the XML node whose content
                     should be output.
                     The case sensitivity for <xpath> is always relevant.
                     If the selected XML node was found by <xpath>, its content is returned as STRING. All other
                     XML nodes are ignored.



Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                              81
Create MyConfig - CMC script
6.15 File operations


                   If the XML file or the specified node is not found, then the function returns "null".

                   Note
                   XML node
                   An XML node can be, for example, an element, an attribute or text.

                   Note
                   XML node <xpath> return
                   If several XML nodes selected by <xpath> are found, only the content of the first XML node is
                   returned.

                   Note
                   Use of environment variables
                   Environment variables of the runtime system can be used in the <path> argument.

                   Note
                   Return value "null"
                   By checking the return value for "null", it can be determined whether the function could not find
                   the file or the XML node.

                   Note
                   Warning in the logbook if the file is not an XML file
                   If the specified file is not an XML file, the function behaves as if the specified path is invalid.
                   The function provides the return value "null" and writes the message of the invalid path as
                   warning in the logbook.




Command line example
                   Up.valCustomerId = QueryXml( "/user/sinumerik/hmi/data/version/
                   identity.xml", "/Config_Identity/Addresses/Manufacturer/ Customer-
                   Id/text()")

6.15.8          TraceToFile


TraceToFile("<path>", "<string>")
                   The TraceToFile() procedure adds a <string> character string to a <path> file.
                   In principle, this procedure can be called in all "dialog scripts", "action scripts", scripts and
                   "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                   If the file does not exist, it is created by the procedure. If the file already exists, the text is
                   added at the end of the file.
                   The <path> argument specifies the file with path and name.
                   The path specification <path> can be relative to the package or absolute, but always refers
                   to the runtime system of the package execution.
                   The use of environment variables is possible. Observe the case sensitivity under Linux.
                   The text including a line feed to be written to the file via the <string> argument is added at
                   the end of the file:
                   • \r\n = CRLF = 0D0A under Microsoft Windows
                   • \n = LF = 0A under Linux
                   The text may include characters of the UTF-8 character set.

                   Note
                   Possible uses
                   The TraceToFile() procedure only works in the runtime system (RTS) of the package
                   execution and therefore has a high performance. You can use the procedure, for example, to
                   write information from the package execution in an uncomplicated way to a file.




Example 1 of TraceToFile
                   TraceToFile("D:\Text.txt", "This is only the first test.")


Example 2 of TraceToFile
                   The channel name and the name of the first geometry axis are written to a CSV file.

                   Up.file = "Test.csv"
                   Up.i = 1
                   If FileExist(RTS, Up.file)
                    FileDelete(RTS, Up.file) ; New CSV should be created
                   EndIf
                   TraceToFile(Up.file, "Channel name; 1st geometry axis") ; header line
                   While Up.i < NC[C1].$ON_NUM_CHANNELS

6.16             XML manipulation
                     Every function opens, manipulates and closes the specified XML file.
                     • For all functions with return value int: Return value 0 if successful
                     • For all functions with return value string: In the case of an error, the function returns "zero".
                     • Restriction:
                        – It is not possible to manipulate individual values. If multiple elements are found with
                          XPath, then indexing is not available in XPath.
                        – Namespaces are not supported. It is not permissible that the XML document itself
                          contains a namespace definition.
                     • If no element in XML matches <xpath expression>, then all functions return an error.

                     • path - path of the XML file

                       The XPath expression can include an attribute reference for the selection.
                     • NewElement - element to be inserted


Example
                     <ToolUserConfig>
                       <ToolUser_4>

                  • path - path of the XML file
                  • xpath_expression - XPath expression
                    The XPath expression can include an attribute reference for the selection.
                  • index - position of the inserted element
                  • NewElement - element to be inserted

6.17           PLC ConfigData manipulation


Changing PLC configuration data
                  PLC configuration data can be changed using the CMC script.
                  CMC Expert provides the PLC configuration data in dialog "System configuration" > "PLC
                  configuration data".
                  The changes take place in the work memory. After the step tree has been executed, the PLC
                  configuration data are written back and transferred to the PLC.




6.17.1         ConfigDataItemExists
                  The function checks whether the specified element exists in the PLC configuration data.
                  Return value: int
                  • 0 - element exists
                  • Error code - element does not exist or no PLC configuration data available


Syntax
                  int ConfigDataItemExists("dbname", "itemName")




                                                                                    Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
96                                                                       Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                         Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                                   6.17 PLC ConfigData manipulation


Arguments
                     • dbName - name of the data block
                     • itemName - name of the element in the data block


See also
                     Examples (Page 98)




6.17.2           ReadConfigDataItem
                     The function lists the content of the specified element.
                     Return value: string
                     An empty string is returned if the element does not exist, or no PLC configuration data is
                     available.


Syntax
                     string ReadConfigDataItem("dbname", "itemName")


Arguments
                     • dbName - name of the data block
                     • itemName - name of the element in the data block


See also
                     Examples (Page 98)




6.17.3           SetConfigDataItem
                     The function changes the content of the specified element. If the element does not exist then
                     it is created.
                     Return value: int
                     • 0 - content was changed or element with content was created
                     • Error code - no PLC configuration data available or element type is not supported
                     If the element does not exist in the PLC, then the PLC rejects it when it is read-in.


Syntax
                     int SetConfigDataItem("dbName", "itemName", "itemType", "value")

Arguments
                  • dbName - name of the data block
                  • itemName - name of the element in the data block
                  • itemType - type of the element in the data block
                  • value - content of the element


See also
                  Examples (Page 98)




6.17.4         RemoveConfigDataItem
                  The function removes the specified element from the PLC configuration data.
                  The function does not remove any element from the PLC. The element is only removed from
                  the set that is used to update the PLC configuration data.
                  Return value: int
                  • 0 - element was removed
                  • Error code - element was not found or no PLC configuration data available


Syntax
                  int RemoveConfigDataItem("dbname", "itemName")


Arguments
                  • dbName - name of the data block
                  • itemName - name of the element in the data block


See also
                  Examples (Page 98)
