6.18           Dialogs
                  You can call the functions and procedures subsequently listed in this section as dialogs on the
                  user interface of the package execution and in "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".




                                                                                     Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
100                                                                       Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                                                              6.18 Dialogs


                     The dialogs provide operators with information - or ask information from operators.

                     Note
                     Straight quotation marks
                     If user interface texts or string values in a function or procedure contain straight quotation
                     marks " ", the straight quotation marks must be enclosed within single quotation marks '"'.
                     In order that they are not interpreted by Create MyConfig, as is also usual in the NC.
                     Examples:
                     Msg("Component '"'HMI Install'"'...")
                     TraceToFile(Up.File,"Up.Text='"'my text'"'")

                     Note
                     Incorrect formatting
                     If an error occurs when formatting texts, e.g. because you did not close a "tag" or wrote it
                     incorrectly, this can lead to the entire formatting of the logbook being altered or corrupted
                     starting at this error location.

                     Note
                     Line breaks and text formatting
                     Line breaks can be inserted in the user interface texts via '<br>'.
                     You can format texts. You can find more information in Section "Text formatting options
                     (Page 113)".

                     Note
                     Handling special characters in strings
                     The straight quotation mark " is enclosed by inverted commas '"' within a string, but only counts
                     as one character.
                     You can only individually insert special characters for line feed '\n' and carriage return '\r' in
                     character strings using a string concatenation operator (Page 69) <<. These characters also only
                     count as one character.

6.18.4           Introduction input functions
                     2 types of input functions are available:
                     • Input functions that are not linked to a particular type
                     • Input functions that are linked to a particular type

                     Input functions linked to a particular type return a typical value, contrary to input
                     functions that are not linked to a particular type:
                     • "string"
                     • "integer"
                     • "real"
                     • Enumerator value as "string"
                     • "unsigned integer"
                     The type-specific input functions require a default value. The user-specified value can be
                     specified directly or applied only at runtime via variables.
                     All of the input functions are always displayed in the "Step tree", independent of the "Display
                     messages" selection.

                     Default value
                     The arguments of the type-specific input functions must include a default value so that
                     fully automatic package execution is possible without requiring any operator action. You can
                     change this default value when manually executing the package.




6.18.5           Input


Input("<label>")
                     The Input() function is a non-type-specific function.
                     In principle, this function can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts"
                     and "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".

                  You query a value during script execution using the Input() function.
                  Whereby, the entered value determines the type. Only enter values that correspond to a
                  permissible type, e.g. "1"; "5", "8"; "0x0"; "Test", true,....
                  If you do not enter any values, the function returns "null". You can intercept this in the
                  script code.
                  You explain the entry using argument <label>.

6.18.6         InputChoice


InputChoice("<label>", "<button1>;<button2>")
                  During package execution, the InputChoice() function displays a dialog with icons.
                  In principle, this function can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts"
                  and "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                  In the dialog, you can make a direct selection by pressing individual buttons.
                  The selection that is made is returned as a character string (the button labeling).
                  The entry is explained using the <label> argument. Optionally, select an icon that
                  is displayed in the dialog during package execution in the argument <label>, at the
                  beginning separated by a semicolon.

                  The following icons <label> are available:
                  •     Selection without icon
                  • *I; selection with "Information" icon
                  • *Q; selection with "Question mark" icon
                  • *W; selection with "Warning" icon
                  • *E; selection with "Error" icon




                                                                                          Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
104                                                                            Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                          Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                                                           6.18 Dialogs


                     The <button> argument is used to specify the identifiers for several buttons, separated by
                     semicolons.
                     2 semicolons in a row cause a line feed, i.e. all of the subsequently listed buttons are
                     displayed in a new line. In this way, buttons can also be arranged one below the another.
                     The freely selectable identifiers simultaneously define the possible return values of the
                     function.

                     Control characters in the <button> argument:
                     • * Accept / input
                     • ^ Reject / cancel with ESC
                     • & Alt-Shortcut
                     The control characters '*‘ and '^‘ can be used to specify the default button for confirming or
                     for cancelling with ESC at the beginning of an identifier.
                     Control character '&' in the identifier for buttons defines the subsequent letters as "Alt-
                     shortcut" (shortcut Alt+<letter>).
                     During package execution, each button can also be operated via the keyboard, using the
                     uniquely assigned keyboard shortcut. Ensure an unambiguous letter assignment across all
                     buttons.
                     The "Alt-shortcuts" are not case sensitive.


Example, selection without icon
                     Up.ret = InputChoice("Example without icon", "*&OK")




                     Figure 6-6   Example without icon



Example, selection with "Information" icon
                     Up.retI = InputChoice("*I; Example of icon '"'Information'"'",
                     "*&OK")




                     Figure 6-7   Example of an "Information" icon

6.18.7           InputEnum


InputEnum("<label>", "*<enum1>;<enum2>")
                     During package execution, function InputEnum() displays a dialog. You can make a selection
                     in the dialog.
                     In principle, this function can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts"
                     and "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                     The selected STRING is assigned to an Up variable.
                     • You can explain the entry using argument <label>.
                     • The selected text sequences can be defined using the <enums n> argument, each separated
                       with a semicolon. Any number can be selected.
                     • You can define this as preselection with a "*" at the beginning of a selected text sequence. If
                       you choose not to do this, then the first listed is preselected.
                     • The return value is the text that the user had selected as string.

Return()
                     The Return() procedure can be used in all scripts to terminate the current script execution.

                  The operating principle of the Return() procedure for dialog scripts, scripts in steps and
                  action scripts is described in CMC Expert in the sections under:
                  • Dialog scripts (Page 258)
                  • Scripts in steps (Page 342)
                  • "Actions" > "Action scripts (Page 353)"
                  Using the procedure in a "CMC script in CMC Diff (Page 170)" also terminates the execution.




6.19.2         ExtCall


ExtCall("<path>")
                  The ExtCall() procedure calls an external CMC script.
                  Procedure ExtCall() can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts" and
                  "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                  For this task, no "check run" is performed in CMC Expert and therefore the syntax is not
                  checked.
                  The file must be stored in UTF-8 coding. You can specify the path either in absolute or relative
                  terms.
                  A relative path refers to the folder from which the package is executed.
                  An absolute path must correspond to the conventions of the runtime system.


Example
                  Extcall("./Data_X_Axis.upscr")
                  The corresponding script can be edited in the integrated "Script Editor" of CMC Expert.

                  Note
                  Using third-party editors for CMC
                  A third-party editor can be used for CMC. Make sure that you use ASCII encoding or UTF-8
                  encoding (without BOM) when saving the file. Use UTF-8 encoding as soon as you use accented
                  characters and special characters outside the ASCII 7-bit character set in the code characters.

6.19.3           Redo


Redo()
                     The Redo() procedure is used in dialog scripts for "OnNext" and "OnEnd" to repeat the inputs
                     in the dialog or the complete dialog processing.

                     Note
                     "OnInit" action
                     It is not permissible to use OnInit in "dialog scripts", in "action scripts" or in "CMC scripts in
                     CMC Diff".


                     The Redo() procedure should preferably be used in the dialogs in the "OnNext" event for
                     monitoring manual entries.

                     More information
                     More information can be found in CMC Expert in the following section:
                     • "Dialog scripts" > "Executing scripts in the dialog pages (Page 258)"




6.19.4           Skip


Skip()
                     You use the Skip() procedure in "dialog scripts" to terminate a dialog.
                     The use of Skip() in a script in the step tree causes the step with the associated actions and
                     substeps to be terminated. The execution continues at the same level in the following step.
                     In "Action scripts" you use Skip() to skip an action.
                     Using Skip() in a "CMC script in CMC Diff" results in the script being terminated. The
                     principle of operation is identical to Return().

                     More information
                     More information can be found in CMC Expert in the following sections:
                     • Dialog scripts (Page 258)
                     • Scripts in steps (Page 342)
                     • "Actions" > "Action scripts (Page 353)"
                     More information can be found in CMC Diff in the following section:
                     • CMC scripts in CMC Diff (Page 170)

6.19 Miscellaneous


6.19.5         DateTime


DateTime("<dt>")
                  The DateTime() function allows the determination and use of the current date and the current
                  time.
                  In principle, this function can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts"
                  and "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                  The <dt> argument informs the function about the format in which the date and time is
                  provided. Examples are provided below.
                  When calling the function without an argument, i.e. with an empty string " " for <dt>, the
                  date and time are formatted according to ISO 8601 "yyyy-MM-ddThh:mm:ss".
                  Also observe uppercase/lowercase within the <dt> argument.


Example
                  To generate a unique name for the logbook, proceed as follows, for example:
                  Up.dt = DateTime("yyyy-MM-dd.hh-mm-ss")
                  Up.$Dialog.PackageEnd.LogName = "$(Up.$Pack.DeployName)_$(Up.dt)"
                  The file extension "*.exe" or "*.usz" generates the package automatically, depending on the
                  "runtime system" defined in the "configuration (Page 237)".

                  Note
                  You can also assign other files (archives...) with specifically generated names in this way.




Examples of units of time
                  Up.year = DateTime("yyyy") ; the year as four digit number
                  Up.month = DateTime("MM") ; the month as number with a leading zero
                  (01-12)
                  Up.day = DateTime("dd") ; the day as number with a leading zero (01
                  to 31)
                  Up.hour = DateTime("hh") ; the hour with a leading zero (00 to 23)
                  Up.minute = DateTime("mm") ; the minute with a leading zero (00 to
                  59)
                  Up.second = DateTime("ss") ; the second with a leading zero (00 to
                  59)
                  Up.milliseconds = DateTime("zzz") ; the milliseconds with leading
                  zeroes (000 to 999)
                  Up.dt = DateTime("yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm:ss.zzz") ; previous examples in
                  combination

6.19.6           DOVar
                     The DOVar() function generates DO variables during package execution in the script,
                     irrespective of the "SINAMICS topology" dialog page.
                     In principle, this function can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts"
                     and "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                     This requires that a SINAMICS has been commissioned without any faults/errors and there is a
                     functioning axis-drive assignment.
                     Use the function in packages only on the "Step tree" dialog page in action scripts or scripts.
                     Then use DO variables and their properties as usual. For example, you can work with DO
                     variables even if there is an update in the field and the topology is "unknown".
                     To generate the DO variables, the user only has to know the DO name ("X-Axis").


DOVar("<doname>")
                     Generates a DO variable using the specified DO name <doname> from "X-Axis".

                     Note
                     The DO name <doname> must be used with the correct uppercase/lowercase notation, as in "X-
                     Axis".


                     Example:
                     Up.myVar1 = DoVar("X-Axis")




6.19.7           Log


Log ("<label>")
                     The Log() procedure writes a user text to the logbook.
                     In principle, this procedure can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts"
                     and "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                     Any message text that is only written in the logbook represents the <label> argument.
                     During package execution the text is not displayed.


Example
                     Giving the logbook entries a "yellow" background makes the logbook easier to read.
                     Log("<span style='background-color:#FFFF99'>My notes in the CMC
                     logbook.</span>")

6.19.9         MathRound


MathRound(<value>, <precision>)
                  You round-off values when calling the MathRound() function.
                  In principle, this function can be called in "dialog scripts", scripts in steps, "action scripts" and
                  "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                  The <value> argument describes the identifier whose value is to be rounded.

                  Examples of identifiers:
                  • Up variables
                  • Machine data
                  • NC data
                  • Drive data
                  Use the <precision> argument to specify the number of digits for rounding. The rounded
                  value is assigned to the specified variable. All identifiers are permitted as variables, whose
                  values can be derived from the corresponding result format of the function, e.g. Up variables,
                  machine data, NC data, drive data.


Example

                  MathRound(<value>, <precision>)
                           Up.pVerst = mathround(0.12345, 3) -> 0.123
                           Up.pVerst = mathround(p1460[0], 2) -> 0.62




                                                                                          Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
124                                                                            Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - CMC script
                                                                                                      6.19 Miscellaneous


Mathematical/scientific rounding off
                     For mathematical/scientific rounding, rounding down is realized if the number of the first
                     decimal place to be eliminated is a 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4. If the number of the first decimal place to be
                     eliminated is a 6, 7, 8 or 9, then the number is rounded up. If the number of the first decimal
                     place that is eliminated is a 5, then the number is rounded-up, if the following additional
                     numbers are not all zero. If the number of the first decimal place that is eliminated is a 5, and all
                     following numbers are zero, then the number is rounded off so that the last number is an even
                     number.

                     Examples for mathematical/scientific rounding off to two decimal places
                     12.62499 ≈ 12.62
                     12.62500 ≈ 12.62
                     12.62501 ≈ 12.63
                     12.63500 ≈ 12.64




6.19.10          Version


Version(<area>, "<app>")
                     You determine the version of an installed application using function Version().
                     In principle, this function can be called in all "dialog scripts", scripts in steps and "action
                     scripts"; however, not in "CMC scripts in CMC Diff".
                     The <area> argument specifies from which control area the version is determined. Possible
                     values for <area> are NCU or PCU.
                     For package area PCU, all SIEMENS applications installed on the
                     PCU, which have been entered in the PCU registry with key
                     "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Siemens\AUTSW", are determined.
                     For package area NCU/PPU, the versions are determined from the "/siemens/
                     versions.xml" file.
                     The <app> argument specifies the application whose version is queried. If the version of the
                     specified application <app> cannot be determined, then the function returns value "null".
                     This means that a response is also issued when a version is not found.
                     For the name of the application <app>, an abbreviated, unambiguous specification is
                     sufficient, e.g. "SINUMERIK CNC" instead of "SINUMERIK CNC-SW 31-5".

                     Note
                     All applications that are found are displayed on the "Version Display" dialog page.

6.20 Preprocessor


6.20           Preprocessor


6.20.1         #Include instruction


#include "<path>"
                    The #include instruction is a deployment directive.
                    These directives can be called in all scripts, dialog scripts and action scripts; only "CMC scripts
                    in CMC Diff" are excluded.
                    You can use relative paths in include statements in scripts.
                    You specify the file path of the external file <path> to be included in relative or absolute
                    terms.
                    Note that the paths refer to the following folders depending on the script type:
                    • For dialog scripts and scripts in the step tree, the relative path refers to the project folder.
                    • For linked dialog scripts/scripts in the step tree, the relative path refers to the folder where the
                      script is saved.
                    • For action scripts, the relative path refers to the folder where the action is saved.
                       – This also applies to linked actions.
                       – This also applies in the task of an action of type "Create with preprocessor".
                       – If the task in an action of type "Create with preprocessor" is linked, then the relative path
                         refers to the task folder.
                    The path can contain Microsoft Windows environment variables, e.g. %SUB_PATH%.
                    The validity of the include statement is checked:
                    • The files to be included are also checked by the check run ("Review project" button).
                    • When creating a package, the contents of the external file are taken over in the script instead
                      of the include statement.

                    Example
                    Log("Include script relative to the project directory")


                    #include "..\ExternalScripts\includable.upscr"


                    Log("Include script with user defined environment variable")


                    #include "%USERVAR%\includable.upscr"


                    Log("Main Script content")

7.1              Introduction

                     Note
                     Documentation structure: Operating Manual / Online Help
                     The contents of Section Create MyConfig - Diff are identical in the Operating Manual and the
                     online help.


                     CMC Diff is software for displaying and comparing SINUMERIK archives, folders, general and
                     special files of the SINUMERIK ONE controller.
                     You can also change and save SINUMERIK archives with CMC Diff.
                     From Create MyConfig V6.10, editing arc archives is no longer supported.
                     Selected data can be exported from SINUMERIK archives or data can be imported into
                     SINUMERIK archives.

                     CMC Diff comprises the following 3 components:

                     • SINUMERIK archive com‐ →        Display and comparison of NC, drive or display data from
                       parison (Page 128)              SINUMERIK archives or files.
                     • Folder comparison      →        Display and comparison of folders, SINUMERIK archives and
                       (Page 173)                      archives in ZIP, TGZ and TAR format.
                     • File comparison        →        Display and comparison of files.
                       (Page 188)
                     The 3 software components of CMC Diff can be called individually and any number of times
                     in the application and are each displayed as a tab.
                     The CMC Diff software can be used to support the configuration of packages with
                     CMC Expert, as well as standard comparison software, independently of CMC Expert.
                     In all 3 components, you can edit the opened archives, folders or files.
                     The data determined with CMC Diff is provided in such a way that it can be incorporated
                     directly into a project.
                     The advantage of CMC Diff that makes it so unique is the fact that it can process SINUMERIK
                     archives, special SINUMERIK files and SINUMERIK data structures.

Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                     127
Create MyConfig - Diff
7.2 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                   CMC Diff shows NC and drive data in a structured fashion in the SINUMERIK archive
                   comparison.

                   Note
                   Representation of non-standard values
                   In the current version, CMC Diff only displays non-standard values from the archive that has been
                   read in.
                   However, it is possible to copy the machine data from another archive. To do this, copy the value
                   from the archive, and insert the value in CMC Diff in the "Edit mode" under tab "Selective". Then
                   change the value.
                   This means that machine data in the archive can be changed.




7.1.1           Network protocol SSH

                   Note
                   Network protocol SSH / archive exchange format DSF
                   To access the NCU or the IPC, programs CMC Shield, CMC Diff and CMC Topo use network
                   protocol "SSH".
                   As standard, the SSH protocol is only available on the NCU as well as Microsoft Windows 10 and
                   Windows 11 systems.
                   Use the archive exchange format "DSF" for exchanging data between other systems/participants.




7.2             SINUMERIK archive comparison


7.2.1           General information on the SINUMERIK archive comparison
                   Any number of comparison objects, e.g. SINUMERIK archives or sub files, can be imported,
                   displayed and compared in a SINUMERIK archive comparison.
                   The comparison is realized at the data level.

                   The SINUMERIK archive comparison supports the comparison of the following objects:
                   • SINUMERIK ONE archives in the DSF format
                   • Drive archives in ASCII and ACX format
                   • NC/drive/display data files (INI, OPT, TEA…) in ASCII format
                   • Data nodes within a comparison object
                   The SINUMERIK archive comparison extracts the NC, drive, and display data from the
                   SINUMERIK archives and displays this data in a structured fashion.


                                                                                       Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
128                                                                         Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                  7.2 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                     Unlike file comparison involving INI files, data is not compared line by line, but according
                     to its identifiers. If the same identifiers occur a multiple number of times, these are only
                     displayed once. The value of the last identifier that was imported is used.
                     The SINUMERIK archive comparison can be performed between different objects opened for
                     comparison, but also within one object (selective).
                     The comparison result is prepared in a structured fashion.
                     You can copy data from the objects being compared to the clipboard and use it in other
                     applications (CMC Expert, ...).
                     You can remove or insert identifiers; you can also change the values of existing identifiers for
                     SINUMERIK archives.
                     CMC Diff allows an open SINUMERIK archive with modified data to be again saved as
                     SINUMERIK archive.

                     Note
                     In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, CMC Diff always displays all data contained in the
                     comparison object if no settings were made in the comparison configuration to exclude data
                     (Expert list or filter).
                     For SINAMICS drive data, there are parameters (r or p) that can be displayed online on the HMI.
                     However, they are not part of an archive and therefore cannot be displayed by CMC Diff.

                     The following main menus and submenus are provided in the SINUMERIK archive
                     comparison:
                     • File
                     • Edit
                     • View
                     • Comparison
                     • Tools
                     • Window
                     • Help

Description of the areas/functions in the SINUMERIK archive comparison window

                      ① Tab "Data view"
                      In the "Data view" tab, you can display the data in 2 different views: in the Normal or
                      Selective mode. To do this, toggle between the 2 "Normal" and "Selective" tabs.
                      By switching over the tab, you can set an opened archive from "Data view" to "Directory
                      view". As a consequence, you do not have to additionally open Folder comparison.

                      ② "Directory view" tab
                      The folder structure of an archive is displayed in the "Directory view".
                      In representation and functionality, the "Directory view" in the SINUMERIK archive
                      comparison corresponds to the folder comparison (Page 173).

142                                                                                  Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                 Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                  7.2 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                     By switching over the tab, you can set an opened archive from "Directory view" to "Data view".

                     ③ Edit mode button
                     The Edit mode can be activated or deactivated by clicking the button. You can only make
                     changes, delete values and add values or identifiers in the "Data view" or "Directory view"
                     tabs when the Edit mode is activated. You must deactivate the Edit mode to toggle between
                     these tabs.

                     Note
                     The NC root files "*.ini" and the drive data "*.tea" cannot be edited.
                     From Create MyConfig V6.10, editing arc archives is no longer supported.


                     ④ "Normal" tab
                     In this area, the data nodes of the comparison objects are shown in a tree structure in the
                     "Normal" comparison mode.
                     In the "Normal" comparison mode, the data structures of all comparison objects (archives,
                     files) are placed one on top of the other and the comparison result is visualized using special
                     node icons.
                     For example, the NC data of axis 1 (AX1) is always compared with the data of axis 1 or the
                     data of drive object 2 (DO2) compared with the data of drive object 2 of another archive.
                     The data structure is formed from all of the data end nodes involved in the comparison of the
                     objects.
                     In this mode, the end nodes of all comparison objects that are located within the selected
                     folder are compared with one another.

                     Table 7-8     Meaning of the icons

                          The equal character in the area node indicates that the data of the objects being compared
                          is identical below this area node.
                          The unequal character in the area node indicates that not all of the data of the objects
                          being compared is identical below this area node.
                          The equal character in the end node indicates that the data of the objects being compared
                          is identical within the end node.
                          The unequal character in the end node indicates that not all of the data of the objects being
                          compared is identical within the end node.
                     The values specified in brackets after a data node specify how many identifiers of a node are
                     displayed and how many identifiers there are in a node.

                   ⑤ "Selective" tab
                   In this area, the data nodes of the comparison objects are shown in a tree structure in the
                   "Selective" comparison mode.
                   In the "Selective" comparison mode, the data structures of all comparison objects, such as
                   archives and files, are placed one below the other. The structure is separately established for
                   every comparison object.
                   Contrary to the "Normal" comparison mode, in the "Selective" comparison mode, all data end
                   nodes of the same type can be compared with one another as required.
                   You can select the data that you want to compare by activating the end nodes.

                   ⑥ Extend selection / Reduce selection buttons
                   "Expand selection" / "Expand All": You can either display a selected folder or the complete
                   data view with all subfolders and nodes in the tree structure.
                   "Reduce selection" / "Reduce all": You can either reduce the selected folder or the complete
                   data view to the main folder. As a consequence, all subfolders and nodes are then no longer
                   visible.

                   ⑦ Display result: Different / Equal / Not available in all comparison objects
                   These values provide information as to how many identifiers in the comparison results have
                   unequal (red) or equal (black) values or which values do not exist in all comparison objects
                   (blue/green arrows).

                   ⑧ Expert list and Filter configurations
                   If the functions "Expert list" and "Filter" are active in the comparison configuration, the
                   relevant icons will be displayed.
                   Double-clicking the icons opens the expert list or filter in the comparison configuration.

                   Note
                   Using "Expert list" and "Filter," you can exclude non-relevant identifiers from the comparison, so
                   that these are no longer displayed.


                   ⑧ Display of the comparison configuration
                   The comparison configuration that is being used in the current comparison is displayed in
                   this field.
                   The comparison configuration is opened with a double-click.

7.2 SINUMERIK archive comparison


Value comparison tab
                   In the "Value comparison" tab, the value-based comparison of floating-point numbers is
                   displayed at significant digits.




                   Figure 7-8   Value comparison tab

                   Floating point numbers are saved separately and internally in the computer in mantissa and
                   exponent.
                   The exponent is adapted in such a way that the mantissa is normalized, i.e. in the range of
                   "1 <= m < 10".
                   The maximum possible number of significant digits is therefore "7" for floating values and 15
                   for double values.
                   Other inaccuracies can occur as a result of parameter calculations, which can be consciously
                   ignored during the comparison.
                   When the comparison algorithm is activated, the difference of the values is normalized using
                   the absolute value of the values. If this is then less than the specified significant digit (the
                   mantissa), then the values are considered equal.


Comment tab
                   Any comments for the selected comparison configuration can be saved in the "Comment" tab.

7.2.4            Copying/exporting data from the SINUMERIK archive comparison
                     In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, data identifiers and the associated values can be copied
                     to the clipboard or exported to a file.
                     For instance, you can use copied or exported data in scripts of CMC Expert, in Microsoft
                     Excel for documentation, in another software application or also in a SINUMERIK archive
                     comparison in CMC Diff.
                     In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, depending on the data marking, there are 2 different
                     copy and/or export formats:
                     • Value assignment
                     • Value table


Copy/export format "Value assignment"
                     For the copy/export format "Value assignment", data is extracted in the form "identifier = value".
                     This means that data is extracted with unique, fully qualified identifiers, a value for each
                     identifier as well as information about the source data area - and is saved in a form that you can
                     directly use in scripts of CMC Expert.
                     This type of copying and exporting is the most frequently applied type.
                     To copy or export data, select the values in the value column as shown below.




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                         153
Create MyConfig - Diff
7.2 SINUMERIK archive comparison


Example 1: Copying SINAMICS data




                   Using the "Copy" or "Data export to file..." shortcut menu entries, you can transfer the
                   selected values and their identifiers to the clipboard or a file.

                   For the selection shown, the following content is obtained for the clipboard or file:

                    [B3_S3_PS3] ;V2.40.43.00
                    p45=1
                    p100=0
                    p105=1

                   A section with the information about the data source is provided in the first line.
                   This information is saved in an CMC Expert-conform format so that it can be used in a script
                   as "Data target" for the following values.
                   The SINAMICS version – from which the following data comes – is saved after the section,

7.2.6            Data tasks in the SINUMERIK archive comparison


7.2.6.1          Overview
                     In the SINUMERIK archive comparison, using data tasks, data can be converted, imported and
                     exported.
                     A configuration and a Microsoft Excel template belong to a data task.


Constraints for data tasks
                     • Data tasks are only available in the "Selective" comparison mode.
                     • Data tasks can only be applied to data end nodes.


Application examples for data tasks
                     • Importing encoder data.
                       Encoder data saved in a Microsoft Excel file (template) can be imported into an archive.
                     • Exporting optimization data.
                       For the identifiers of optimization data saved in a Microsoft Excel template, values can be
                       added and saved as Microsoft Excel file.


Principle of operation of import tasks
                     When executing import tasks, values are imported into the clipboard from the "Import area" of
                     a Microsoft Excel template.
                     In CMC Diff, these values can be inserted at a data end node. When inserting values, the
                     values of existing identifiers can be overwritten and new identifiers can be inserted.


Principle of operation of export tasks
                     When executing export tasks, data identifiers are determined in an "Export area" of a Microsoft
                     Excel template. These identifiers are searched for in a selected data end node in the data
                     structure of the SINUMERIK archive comparison and their values are transferred into a Microsoft
                     Excel template.
                     The "Save as" dialog allows you to save the filled Microsoft Excel template.


Principle of operation of conversion tasks
                     When executing conversion tasks, data identifiers are determined from an "Export area" of a
                     Microsoft Excel template. These identifiers are searched for in a selected data end node in the
                     data structure of the SINUMERIK archive comparison and their values are transferred into a
                     Microsoft Excel template.
                     The conversion rule stored in the same Microsoft Excel template is processed by Microsoft
                     Excel without visualization. In so doing, values are generated for the saved import identifiers
                     and these are then imported to CMC Diff from the "Import area". The imported values are
                     saved in the clipboard, and can be inserted into CMC Diff at a data end node.

7.2.8           CMC scripts in CMC Diff


7.2.8.1         Introduction


Analysis and manipulation of archives using CMC scripts in CMC Diff
                   CMC Diff supports the advanced analysis and manipulation of archives via CMC script. You can
                   implement, for example, complex data export operations using the script functions to write to
                   files. A command line interface for executing the CMC scripts in CMC Diff is provided for
                   automation tasks.
                   From Create MyConfig V6.10, editing arc archives is no longer supported.

                   Note
                   License
                   You require a license to use CMC scripts in CMC Diff.
                   The function as extension "Create MyConfig ADDON /DIFF SCRIPTING" is under license.




More information
                   In CMC Diff you can apply CMC scripts on SINUMERIK archives.
                   Complex and controlled data exports from archives are possible, without having to generate
                   a CMC package. You can also manipulate the data archive.
                   You can start the scripts from the CMC Diff interface - or using a command line call.

                   Note
                   Exceptions for CMC scripts in CMC Diff
                   "CMC scripts in CMC Diff" are subject to restrictions.
                   Details on this are provided in the section or in the online help "Create MyConfig CMC script
                   (Page 35)".




More information on CMC scripts
                   More information about "CMC scripts" is provided in Section "Create MyConfig CMC script
                   (Page 35)" in the Operating Manual or in the online help with the same name.


7.2.8.2         Data accesses / sections / identifiers
                   You must always use fully qualified sections to be able to read and write access archived data,
                   e.g. NC[C1], PS[B3_S3_PS3].
                   Use simple identifiers under fully qualified sections.
                   You only use fully qualified identifiers for read access operations.



                                                                                        Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
170                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                 Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                  7.2 SINUMERIK archive comparison


                     Example
                     NC[C1] ;Fully qualified section
                     $MC_CHAN_NAME=InputText("Enter the required channel names:","");
                     simple identifier
                     Up.KName1=$MC_CHAN_NAME ;simple identifier
                     MSG("Channel name for channel 1 was set to $(Up.KName1).")
                     Up.KName2=NC[C2].$MC_CHAN_NAME ;fully qualified identifier
                     MSG("Channel name for channel 2 is $(Up.KName2).")

                     Note
                     No access to display data (HMI) in the archive
                     It is not possible to access display data (HMI) in the archive from CMC scripts in CMC Diff.

                     Note
                     Write access to archive data
                     Activate the "Edit mode" in CMC Diff to write archive data to the CMC script.
                     Check system variable Up.$Script.EditMode to determine if the "Edit mode" is activated




7.2.8.3          System variables
                     More information about system variables of CMC scripts in CMC Diff is provided in Section "CMC
                     script" > "System variables - CMC scripts in CMC Diff" (Page 39) or in the online help "Create
                     MyConfig CMC-Skripte".


7.2.8.4          Calling scripts from the interface

                     Calling scripts using the list of opened archives
                     To call a script in CMC Diff, right-click the required archive in the list of opened comparisons.
                     In the context menu, select either "Data processing with scripts" or "Last scripts used".
                     For read-only access to the archive, the Edit mode must not be switched on. Activate the Edit
                     mode when writing to the archive or making changes in it.
                     A CMC script is executed by CMC Shield.

                                                                                                7.3 Folder comparison


7.3              Folder comparison


7.3.1            General information
                     In a Folder comparison of CMC Diff, you can compare 2 comparison objects with each other,
                     insert or delete files or folders and resave the modified objects. The comparison result is
                     compared on the folder and file levels and then shown. This means that the contents of the files
                     are compared optionally, but not displayed.
                     You can compare and edit the following objects using the Folder comparison:
                     • Folders/directories
                     • SINUMERIK ONE archives in the DSF format
                     • ZIP archives
                     • TGZ archives
                     • TAR archives
                     Because unpacked archives often represent a structure consisting of folders and files, similar
                     rules apply to comparing and editing.
                     In the folder comparison, files with the same name are compared for size, date, version, and
                     binary content.
                     The comparison result is prepared both qualitatively and quantitatively.
                     From the comparison objects, folders and files can be copied to the clipboard and to other
                     applications (CMC Expert, Microsoft Windows Explorer, etc.).




7.3.2            Overview of user interface


7.3.2.1          Main menus
                     The main menus in CMC Diff are identical. The submenus are adapted dynamically to the
                     associated SINUMERIK archive comparison, Folder comparison or File comparison component.

                     The following main menus and submenus are available in the Folder comparison:
                     • File
                     • Edit
                     • View
                     • Comparison
                     • Tools
                     • Window
                     • Help

7.3 Folder comparison


Description of the areas/functions in the Folder comparison window
                   The individual functions of the folder comparison are described in more detail below:

                   ① Folder structure - Representation of the folders with the associated comparison
                   objects in the tree structure
                   In this area, the folders of the comparison objects are shown in a tree structure arranged one
                   on top of the other. The comparison result is visualized using special folder icons.

                   ② Colored comparison of the comparison objects
                   The content of the folder selected in the ① area is displayed next to each other for both
                   comparison objects (②). The center column ③ with the comparison result icons also serves
                   as demarcation between the left-hand and right-hand comparison objects.
                   The comparison results are color-coded to make it easier to interpret the results:
                   • Objects that are only available on the left-hand side are shown in green.
                   • Unequal objects or properties available on both sides are shown in red.
                   • Equal objects or properties available on both sides are shown in black.
                   • Objects that are only available on the right-hand side are shown in blue.
                   The contents of the column can be sorted in ascending or descending order by clicking the
                   column header.

                   Note
                   The contents of the files are only compared in the binary notation if you preselected this in the
                   comparison configuration. More information is provided in the "Configuration (Page 183)".
                   The date for the comparison is not relevant for folders.

                   Note
                   PLC blocks identification
                   If PLC blocks are marked yellow, they are Safety Integrated plus blocks.




                   Figure 7-17   PLC blocks identification - Safety Integrated plus

                   ③ Column of the comparison result icons
                   Column with the comparison result icons, to separate the left-hand and right-hand
                   comparison objects.
                   When the Edit mode is activated, you can change the icons for synchronization purposes by
                   left-clicking or via the shortcut menu.

                     Significance of the comparison icons:

                            A green arrow indicates that the folder is only available in the left-hand comparison
                            object.
                            The unequal character indicates that the contents of the folder are not identical.
                            The equal character indicates that the contents of both folders are identical.
                            A blue arrow indicates that the folder is only available in the right-hand comparison
                            object.

                     ④ Assignment of the comparison results icon/value (status bar bottom right)

                     The value in front of the slash specifies how many of these files can be seen in the selected
                     folder.
                     The value after the slash shows the total number of these files that are contained in both
                     comparison objects.

                     Specifies that there are "8" unequal files from a total of "14" in the currently selected folder.

                     The "Open", "Send to" and "Copy" entries can be used to view and extract files from archives.
                     The entry "Open with file comparison" or a double-click opens the files contained in the
                     selected line in the data comparison of CMC Diff.
                     The other entries can be used to edit a selected file or a selected folder.

                     ⑥ Configure comparison
                     A filter is used in the comparison configuration. More information can be found in Section
                     "Configuration (Page 183)".
                     The comparison configuration is opened with a double-click.

                     Note
                     Using inclusion and exclusion filters, it is possible that not all of the files of the folder or archive
                     are displayed any longer.

                     The comparison configuration that is being used in the current comparison is displayed in
                     this field. More information can be found in Section "Configuration (Page 183)".
                     The comparison configuration is opened with a double-click.

Comparison tab

                     ④ Compare file size
                     For activated size comparison, the size of the files and folders is considered.
                     If you do not activate the option check box, a check is only made whether files and folders
                     exist in both comparison objects.
                     This option is activated as standard.

                     ⑤ Date when file was last saved option button
                     When the date/version comparison is activated, then for this selection, CMC Diff also takes
                     into account the date when the file was last saved - and displays this in either black or red.
                     The date is not relevant for folders.

                     ⑥Option button Date/Version with regular identification expression drop-down list
                     SINUMERIK archives can contain cycles.
                     The cycle version number is specified in the file. When making a comparison, the version
                     number provides more information than the date and can be used for the comparison.
                     In order to be able to compare the version numbers, the files in the first 10 lines are checked
                     for the character string, which is then described using a regular identification expression.
                     A regular expression that is generally used is already selected in the specified comparison
                     configuration "SINUMERIK archives".
                     You can also create user-defined regular expressions in the drop-down list. Information
                     on using regular expressions is provided in Section "Using regular expressions in CMC Diff
                     (Page 214)".

                     ⑦ "Additional comparison criteria" check box
                     The content of the files is only compared byte-by-byte when you select the additional
                     comparison criterion "Compare binary content of the files". Otherwise, only the size and
                     possibly the date and/or the version are compared.

                   Table 7-14     Examples of filters:

                    *.ini                      The "*" (asterisk) expression represents any number of any characters.
                                               If the entry is defined in the inclusion filter, only file names with the file exten‐
                                               sion "ini" are displayed, and all others are hidden. If "*.ini" is present in the
                                               exclusion filter, all file names with the "ini" extension are not displayed.
                    cycle8?.spf                The question mark represents precisely one character (any character).
                                               If you have defined the entry in the inclusion filter, files with the "cycle8" name
                                               plus any arbitrary character and the "spf" file extension are displayed, and all
                                               others are hidden.
                                               File names with the designation "cycle8?.spf" can therefore be called as fol‐
                                               lows: cycle80.spf, cycle81.spf, cycle8a.spf..., etc.

                     Files, folders or complete folder structures can be copied from the comparison objects of the
                     folder comparison to the clipboard and then, e.g. in CMC Expert, inserted in a component.
                     This means that it is possible to extract files from SINUMERIK, ZIP, TAR or TGZ archives,
                     without you having to use software that is not part of the Create MyConfig ecosystem.

7.3.6           Save archive


SINUMERIK DSF archive
                   In SINUMERIK ONE, the "Backup" and "Setup" DSF archives are used and supported over the
                   complete workflow.
                   For CMC, the "Backup" DSF archive is primarily relevant. Control data is backed up and can be
                   restored again.
                   CMC uses setup archives for certain functions. The archive provided by the TIA Portal for
                   configuring the PLC is a setup archive.
                   More information on the DSF archive is provided in the System Manual
                   SINUMERIK ONE Create MyVirtual Machine (https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/ww/en/
                   view/110002278).




7.4             File comparison


7.4.1           General information
                   In a file comparison using CMC Diff, you can compare the contents of two files line by line.
                   The comparison result is processed from qualitative and quantitative perspectives.
                   Contents can be copied from the files line by line to the clipboard and used in other
                   applications (CMC Expert ...).
                   In Edit mode, you can delete lines or characters directly in the file comparison, insert them or
                   copy them backwards and forwards between files.
                   It is also possible to simultaneously and externally process a file opened in the comparison.

                      Gray                        Identical in the relevant part of the line.

                   ④ Comparison result icons and color coding of lines
                   The lines of the files to be compared are displayed next to one another in this area and are
                   color-coded to make it easier to interpret the comparison result.

                               The green arrow and the line number with green background indicate that this line
                               only exists in the left-hand file.
                               The not equal sign and the line numbers with red background indicate that the con‐
                               tent of the line is not identical.
                               The black equals sign indicates that both lines are identical.
                               The gray equals sign indicates that the relevant part of the line match.
                               The blue arrow and the line number with blue background indicate that this line only
                               exists in the right-hand file.

                   Note
                   Non-relevant parts of a line, e.g. spaces or comments, can be defined in the comparison
                   configuration.
                   More information can be found in Section "Configuration (Page 197)".




                   Note
                   Lines or characters shown in gray have been excluded from a comparison by a filter.

7.6 Command line call


Notes

                   Note the following information for the command line call:

                   Note
                   Sequence of the switches
                   Write the switches in the specified sequence.
                   When doing this, note the following "Significance of the switches" table.

                   Note
                   Path data
                   • Paths must be specified in straight quotation marks if spaces are included.
                      Example:
                      "C:\Path with spaces\Expert_Logfile.log"
                   • Paths must never end with '\'.

                   Note
                   Saving batch files
                   Always save batch files with ANSI/ASCII encoding.

                   Note
                   Umlauts and special characters
                   Do not use any umlauts (special German characters) and special characters when specifying
                   paths.
                   To allow special characters or umlauts to be correctly processed in specified paths, save the batch
                   files with command line calls with the same character set as used by the region-specific
                   command line interpreter "*cmd.exe".
                   For example, Codepage 850, also known as DOS Latin 1, applies for the region Western Europe.
                   The Notepad editor integrated in Microsoft Windows does not support saving files with this
                   character set.

                   Note
                   Uppercase/lowercase
                   For the command line switches and arguments, always use the specified uppercase/lowercase
                   notation.
                   You must observe the case sensitivity for the argument of the "/config" switch.

Example

                   /compare /config "myConfig"




7.7             Using regular expressions in CMC Diff


7.7.1           General information on regular expressions
                   Regular expressions represent a general notation to describe text patterns. They are known as
                   a type of programming language to test and manipulate texts.
                   A regular expression is a character string with syntactic rules which defines significant text
                   patterns or character strings in a general form. Regular expressions are used in CMC Diff to
                   identify a significant character string and to filter it (e.g. all block numbers or all comments in a
                   cycle).
                   A regular expression comprises 2 types of characters:
                   • Literal characters
                   • Meta characters


Literal characters
                   Literal characters are characters that only represent themselves in a regular expression and have
                   no special significance.
                   A search with a regular expression that only contains literals, therefore corresponds to a
                   conventional character search.


Meta characters
                   Meta characters are characters that have a special function within regular expressions.

                   Some meta characters follow:
                   $ ^ { } [ ] ( ) | . * + ? \ -.
                   Similar to natural languages, literals can be considered as being the vocabulary, with meta
                   characters being the grammar of regular expressions.




                                                                                          Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
214                                                                            Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                       Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                                7.7 Using regular expressions in CMC Diff


Escape sequence
                     If a meta character is required as literal character to formulate a regular expression, i.e. it must
                     only stand for itself, then the character must be masked with what is called an escape sequence.
                     This is achieved by prefixing a backslash "\".

                     Example
                     An open square bracket "[" identifies a regular expression.
                     Insert a backslash "\" in front of the square bracket.
                     Because the single square bracket is only a meta character, i.e. has a special function, see
                     character classes.
                     In this case, "\[" is written in the regular expression.




7.7.2            Meta characters in the regular expressions
                     Important meta characters are shown in the following subsections which are contained in the
                     dialect of the regular expressions of Create MyConfig.


Character classes
                     In a regular expression, a character class defines one character, that may be one of the characters
                     contained in the character class.

                      Meta charac‐                                           Description
                      ters
                             .         Corresponds to any character with the exception of \n (line break).
                            [ ]        A character set available for selection is defined using square brackets. The expression
                                       in the square brackets precisely stands for one character from this selection.
                          [acdb]       Corresponds to one single character that is contained in the specified character string.
                                       This means one a, one b, one c or one d. The sequence of the characters within the
                                       character class is of no significance.
                         [^acdb]       Corresponds to any, individual character that is not contained in the specified character
                                       string. If a ^ is not located at the beginning of the definition, then it should be con‐
                                       sidered as literal.
                                       For "character negation" the ^ can only be located within the square brackets and here,
                                       in turn, may only be used at the beginning!
                                       Outside the square bracket, ^ has a different meaning, see below: "Constructs".
                       [0-9a-fAF]      Adjacent characters are specified as a range by using a hyphen.
                                       If the hyphen is written at the beginning or at the end of the character class or with
                                       backslash \-, then it stands for itself and is not valid as specifying a range.
                            \w         A character which is a letter, a number or an underscore.
                            \W         A character which is neither a letter, number nor underscore.
                            \s         Corresponds to any space characters, e. g. space, tab, line feed etc.
                            \S         Corresponds to any non-space characters.
                            \d         Corresponds to any decimal number, corresponds to [0-9].
                            \D         Corresponds to any non number, corresponds to [^0-9].




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                                  215
Create MyConfig - Diff
7.7 Using regular expressions in CMC Diff


                    Meta charac‐                                           Description
                    ters
                           \t       Corresponds to a tab stop character.
                           \n       Corresponds to a line break.
                          \x20      Corresponds to an ASCII character in the hexadecimal notation (precisely two posi‐
                                    tions).
                         \u0020     Corresponds to a unicode character in the hexadecimal notation (precisely four posi‐
                                    tions).



Constructs

                    Meta charac‐                                           Description
                    ters
                           |        Several regular expressions can be combined to form a single one using alternation
                                    (logic OR).
                                    Example: cat|dog|tiger. (cat or dog or tiger)
                                    The match to the far left has priority.
                          ( )       The grouping is used to combine parts of regular expressions and to limit the range of
                                    validity of an alternation.
                                    Example: _(abc|xyz)_
                           ^        The meta character for the beginning of the line does not describe a character, but
                                    instead a position in a line.
                                    Example: ^[aA] requires a lower-case a or an upper-case A at the beginning of the
                                    line.
                                    The ^ character in square brackets has a different meaning, it is used as negation of
                                    the character string.
                           $        The meta character for the end of the line does not describe a character, but instead a
                                    position in a line.
                                    Example: [aA]$ requires a lower-case a or an upper-case A at the end of the line.



Quantifier
                   Quantifiers are used to specify how many times a specific component of a regular expression
                   must occur in order for a found character string to be considered a match. A quantification
                   expression is valid for the character or character set which is located directly in front of it.

                    Meta charac‐                                           Description
                    ters
                           ?        Requires a null or a match.
                                    Example: _? or (abc|xyz)?.
                           +        Requires one or any number of matches. Example: a+ or [0-9]+.
                           *        Requires null or any number of matches.
                                    Example: \w* or (abc)*.
                          {n}       Requires precisely n matches.
                                    Example: (abc){2,}.




                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
216                                                                              Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                     Create MyConfig - Diff
                                                                               7.7 Using regular expressions in CMC Diff


                      Meta charac‐                                         Description
                      ters
                           {n,}        Requires a minimum of n matches, but there can also be more.
                                       Example: (abc){2,}.
                          {n,m}        Requires at least n matches, however a maximum of m matches.
                                       Example: \w {2.17}.




7.7.3            Examples of regular expressions

                      Regular expression     Charac‐   Description
                                             ter
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]                      Describes a section, e.g. [Version]
                                                       At the beginning of the line there should be an "open square brack‐
                                                       et" [ and then there should be at least one character other than a
                                                       "close square bracket" ] followed by a "close square bracket" ].
                                                       The remainder up to the end of the line is not specified.
                      ①②③④⑤...                         Numbers indicate the position of the character in the regular ex‐
                                                       pression.
                      The regular expression is described below from the left to the right:
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ①^        Here, the beginning of the line, i.e. the described expression should
                                                       be located at the beginning of the line.
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ②\        Escape character; the "open square bracket" [ should stand for itself
                                                       as literal and not as meta character of a character set.
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ③[        Character stands for itself, i.e. at the beginning of the line there
                                                       should be an "open square bracket" [.
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ④[        Starting definition of a character set (character is a meta character).
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ⑤^        Here, a negation character, i.e. the characters specified in the char‐
                                                       acter set, should not occur.
                                                       The character negation is only possible within square brackets,
                                                       therefore, brackets are used for characters ④ and ⑧.
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ⑥\        Escape character; the "close square bracket" ] should stand for itself
                                                       as literal and not as meta character of a character set.
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ⑦]        This character stands for itself.
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ⑧]        End definition of a character set
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ⑨+        Requires one match or as many matches as specified, i.e. there must
                                                       be at least one character, which is not a "]".
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ⑩\        Escape character; the "close square bracket" ] should stand for itself
                                                       as literal and not as meta character of a character set.
                      ^\[[^\]]+\]            ⑪]        This character stands for itself.
