7.7 Using regular expressions in CMC Diff



                    Regular expression      Charac‐   Description
                                            ter
                    ^[^=]+=                           Describes a value assignment (identifier = value)
                                                      e. g. Version = 1.0.3
                                                      At the beginning of the line there should be at least one character,
                                                      which is not an equal sign "=". This expression (^[^=]+) stands for
                                                      the "identifier" in the value assignment.
                                                      This should then be followed by an equal sign "=" and the remainder
                                                      of the line, the value, is not specified.
                    ①②③④⑤...                          Numbers indicate the position of the character in the regular ex‐
                                                      pression.
                    The regular expression is described below from the left to the right:
                    ^[^=]+=                 ①^        Here, the beginning of the line, i.e. the described expression should
                                                      be located at the beginning of the line.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ②[        Start of the definition of a character set (character is a meta charac‐
                                                      ter).
                    ^[^=]+=                 ③^        Here, a negation character, i.e. the characters specified in the char‐
                                                      acter set should not occur.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ④=        Equal sign (literal) stands for itself.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ⑤]        End of the definition of a character set.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ⑥+        Requires one match or as many matches as specified, i.e. there must
                                                      be at least one character, which is not an equal sign.
                    ^[^=]+=                 ⑦=        Equal sign (literal) stands for itself.



                    Regular expression        Character           Description
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)                              Describes a CHANDATA instruction in an NC-INI file,
                                                                  e. g. CHANDATA(1)
                                                                  CHANDATA should be at the beginning of the line, fol‐
                                                                  lowed by a "open round bracket", followed by at least one
                                                                  digit, followed by a "close round bracket".
                    ①②③④⑤...                                      Numbers indicate the position of the character in the
                                                                  regular expression.
                    The regular expression is described below from the left to the right:
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ①^                  Here, the beginning of the line, i.e. the described expres‐
                                                                  sion should be located at the beginning of the line.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ②CHANDATA           This literal character stands for itself, i.e. a search is made
                                                                  for a CHANDATA.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ③\                  Escape character; the "open round bracket" should stand
                                                                  for itself as literal and not as meta character of a group.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ④(                  This character stands for itself.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ⑤\d                 Corresponds to any decimal number.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ⑥+                  Requires one match or as many matches as specified, i.e.
                                                                  there must be at least one decimal number.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ⑦\                  Escape character; the "close round bracket" should stand
                                                                  for itself as literal and not as meta character of a group.
                    ^CHANDATA\(\d+\)          ⑧)                  This character stands for itself.

8.1              Layout and operation


8.1.1            Introduction

                     Note
                     Documentation structure: Operating Manual / Online Help
                     The contents of Section Create MyConfig Expert are identical in the Operating Manual and the
                     online help.


                     CMC Expert is the engineering software for creating a CMC project.
                     An executable package for the production or upgrading of machines is generated from the
                     CMC project with the "Create package" function.
                     The package contains a configurable sequence of production or upgrading steps and the
                     associated data.
                     In CMC Expert, you specify the configuration of the package, the dialog for operator
                     interactions and the individual upgrade steps in the form of a hierarchical step tree. You
                     specify the required data or data to be manipulated and files.

                     Project - creating and configuring
                     You can configure the majority of the settings easily in the "Project explorer (Page 226)"
                     • Directly in the dialog "Configuration (Page 237)"
                     • Under "Dialogs (Page 249)" and in the "Step tree (Page 338)"
                     • Via a context-sensitive shortcut menu
                     A "check run (Page 235)" informs you if there are any errors in the configuration.

                     Script Editor
                     CMC Expert provides the integrated "Script Editor" which effectively supports you when
                     creating scripts.

                     Executable package
                     The "Create package" function creates a package that can be executed under Linux or
                     Microsoft Windows depending on the configuration.

                  A CMC Expert project V6.1 and higher can be opened, edited and saved with CMC V6.10.
                  When opening a CMC Expert project from V6.1 and higher, you have to confirm a message.
                  The project is converted and can then be edited.
                  We recommend that you manually back up or archive each project with all of its internal and
                  external components before opening it with the higher CMC version.
                  Projects saved with CMC V6.10 cannot be edited with previous CMC versions.

                  The visibility of the elements defines whether all actions and scripts are visible in the step
                  tree, or only those under the currently selected step. This improves the display of the step
                  tree structure and a larger section of the step tree can be seen in the Project Explorer.
                  This setting is the default setting when opening projects. The representation at the root
                  element in the step tree can be changed via the context menu.

                  Allow editing
                  Editing links in actions that are located outside the project can either be activated or
                  deactivated. With this option, only those actions are edited that are saved in the current
                  Expert version.


Package creation
                  No message in case of changed action content
                  Possible inconsistencies between the content in the actions and the file system lead to
                  messages. This can mean that package creation is unsuccessful
                  When this option is activated, when creating a package no messages are displayed if action
                  content is changed. The package is still created and is generated with the current content of
                  the action directory.

8.1.9           Easy to operate CMC Expert user interface


Arrangement of the viewlets
                    In the default settings of CMC Expert, the content area on the left forms a fixed frame. The
                    "Project explorer" viewlet is next to it and the viewlet properties are located on the right side of
                    the CMC Expert user interface.
                    The "Details" and "Messages" viewlets are located below the Properties viewlet.
                    In CMC Expert you adapt the dockable viewlets to your ambient conditions and the work
                    situation. You can increase or reduce the size of the viewlets as required.
                    This is advantageous for larger projects to improve the overview and readability of a project.
                    The viewlets can be moved to another location in the CMC Expert user interface and
                    redocked via the positioning tiles. The "Project explorer", "Details" and "Messages" viewlets
                    can be removed from the CMC Expert user interface and displayed in a separate window.
                    Dockable viewlets are:
                    • Project explorer
                    • Project management
                    • Messages
                    • Details
                    You can, for example, move the "Project explorer" viewlet to the right.
                    You can move the "Details" and "Messages" viewlets as tabs into the working area and thus
                    toggle between the tabs as needed.

8.3              Managing and using configurations


8.3.1            Overview
                    All settings you define in the property fields under "Configuration", "Dialogs" and "Steps" are
                    configurations.
                    Some of the configurations are shown with system variables and can be written or read
                    subsequently via scripts, e.g. during or before execution.
                    When the term "configurations" is used within this section, just this subset of configurations
                    for which system variables also exist is meant.
                    In this case, the handling of configurations always means the handling of the associated
                    system variables, including their values.


                                                                                           Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
236                                                                             Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                             8.3 Managing and using configurations


                     The system variables for "Configuration", "Dialogs" and "Steps" can be found in the
                     "Properties" of the respective element.

                     Note
                     Reference list, system variables
                     More information on the individual system variables can be found in section "Reference list
                     system variables (Page 373)".


                     The configurations are located in text files with extension "*.upcfg".
                     The format of the text files corresponds to that of a CMC task or a CMC script.
                     Value assignments are made in the form <System variable> = <Value>. Comments
                     are identified by a prefixed semicolon. You can also remove any number of configurations
                     from the configuration files and, for example, so limit the number being used. When loading/
                     using this configuration, only the settings contained in the package are set with all other
                     configurations remaining unaffected. Proceed in this manner when, for example, in an
                     existing package, a switchover is performed only between a new installation and an upgrade
                     for automatic execution.

8.3.4            Password handling in Create MyConfig
                     Password handling in Create MyConfig is based on certain basic principles. Create MyConfig
                     saves each password in a separate, encrypted file. The passwords are thus managed and
                     transported in the form of protected files.
                     In Create MyConfig, a distinction is made between the engineering environment and the
                     runtime environment.



                                                                                                Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
240                                                                                  Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                8.3 Managing and using configurations


Protection classes for password information
                     There are various protection classes for protecting password information.
                     • CMC standard: Obfuscation through a product-global key from CMC
                     • Transport password: Encryption using the transport password
                     Depending on the application, the protection classes are used as follows:
                     • In the engineering environment (CMC Expert project):
                       The password information is concealed by a product-global engineering key from CMC.
                     • In the package generated by CMC Expert:
                        – The password information is concealed by a product-global runtime key from CMC.
                        – Encryption is performed using a user-defined transport password.
                     • Standalone file created using ExpertCmd:
                        – The password information is concealed by a product-global runtime key from CMC.
                        – Encryption is performed using a user-defined transport password.
                     The properties of the protection classes are as follows:
                     • Obfuscation using the product-global runtime key from CMC:
                       An automatic process is possible, as CMC can decrypt the data without user interaction. From
                       a security point of view, however, this is insecure as the decryption information is available
                       in CMC. This also applies to the global engineering key.
                     • Encryption using the transport password:
                       An automatic process is not possible, as entering the corresponding transport password is
                       required for decryption. From a security point of view, this is secure as information from the
                       user is required for decryption. The decryption information is not available in CMC.


Transition from the engineering environment to the package
                     The protection class achieved for the password information in the package is determined based
                     on the settings in the project. The passwords concealed in the engineering environment are
                     recoded according to the protection class achieved.

                     Determining the protection class achieved for the passwords in the package
                     • Transport password if at least one of the following conditions is met:
                        – A transport password is configured.
                        – Authentication is carried out using information available at runtime.
                        – Package generation is executed from the command line and a transport password is
                          specified as a parameter.
                     • Otherwise the runtime obfuscation.

                     Restrictions
                     If transport password is determined as the protection class achieved, all files provided at
                     runtime must have this protection class. Normally, the files are encrypted with the same
                     transport password. However, if files with different transport passwords are used, CMC will




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                       241
Create MyConfig - Expert
8.3 Managing and using configurations


                   ask again for each file if no suitable transport password has been specified during the
                   package run.


See also
                   Manage security settings (Page 240)

8.4              Using language resources


8.4.1            Adding language resources


Adding language resources to the project
                     CMC supports the use of language resources without their management.
                     The language resources can be edited using the CMC Resource Editor.
                     Manual steps are required to integrate language resources.




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                          245
Create MyConfig - Expert
8.4 Using language resources


                  The folder structure and folder names are mandatory.
                  1. In the project folder, create folder "res".
                  2. Create a folder for each language in folder "res".
                     In the example "deu" for German and "eng" for English.
                  3. In folder "res" and in the folders for the particular language, create the files with the language
                     resources.
                     – "Dialog.ts" for the information texts in the dialogs
                     – "Step.ts" for the information texts in the steps
                     – "User.ts" for user-defined texts (used by ResText() (Page 247))
                     – Additional resource files (used by ResFile() (Page 247))




                  The associated file is used for the package execution in accordance with the selected
                  language. When "English" is selected, a search is first made for the file in the corresponding
                  language folder, e.g. "eng". If the file is not found in the language folder, then a search is
                  made one level higher in folder "res" and this is used.

8.4.2            Using function ResFile()


ResFile("<file>")
                     Function ResFile() is for the use or call of text resources in the form of files.
                     To display the content from a file, you can use function ResFile() in the information texts
                     in dialogs and steps as an alternative to plain text. Use in the script is also possible.
                     The file specified using argument <file> must be located in the language folder with the
                     same name. The file must be in the *.txt, *.htm or *.html format.
                     The associated file is used for the package execution in accordance with the selected
                     language. When "German" is selected, a search is first made for the file in the corresponding
                     language folder, e.g. "deu". If the file is not found in the language folder, then a search is
                     made one level higher in folder "res" and this is used.


Example of ResFile()
                     Calling the function in the information text of dialog page "Package configuration":
                     =ResFile("HintForConfiguration.txt")




8.4.3            Using function ResText()


ResText("<resid>"[, "<arg>"]*)
                     Function ResText() calls text resources in the form of information texts from language
                     resource file "User.ts".
                     File "User.ts" is located in each language folder. The texts from the "User.ts" belonging to the
                     language are then used to execute the package corresponding to the selected language.
                     If you work with language-dependent texts, the ResText() function is used in scripts, e.g.
                     messages, input dialogs, etc., as an alternative to plain text.
                     To call the "Information text" of the "User.ts" file, specify the "ID" in the "User.ts" file using the
                     <resid> argument.
                     Up to 9 optional arguments <arg> are possible to transfer variable text components from the
                     script into the calling information text.


Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                              247
Create MyConfig - Expert
8.4 Using language resources


                  As placeholders for the <arg> arguments transferred by the function, the "%1" to "%9"
                  characters are used in the information text of the "User.ts".


Example 1 of ResText()
                  Up.MSG1 = ResText("T1")
                  MSG("$(Up.MSG1)")

8.5.4            Events

                     When creating a new project, the events (Page 254) "OnInit", "OnNext" and "OnEnd" are
                     automatically created for each dialog.

                     Exception
                     No events are created for the following dialogs:
                     • Notes about acknowledgment
                     • Notes on the package
                     • Version Display
                     • Finish
                     You open the events of a dialog by left-clicking on the arrow to the left of the option check
                     box of the dialog.

                  Figure 8-18   Opening events of a dialog

                  You can create or link scripts (Page 258) and steps (Page 338) for every event.

                  Note
                  The project engineer is responsible in defining whether the configured content of an action or
                  a script can be executed at the given location.




8.5.4.1        Meaning of the events
                  The following table describes what you can achieve by using a specific event.

                  Table 8-10    Event - Meaning

                   Event               Meaning / Time of script execution
                   OnInit (Page 255)   The script is executed before the dialog page is displayed.
                                       OnInit is used, for example:
                                       •   To (conditionally) skip this dialog page
                                       •   To issue queries to the operator and process them before the dialog page opens
                                       •   To change settings of this dialog page via system variables based on the current
                                           execution
                   OnNext              The script is executed in the dialog immediately after clicking "Next".
                   (Page 256)          OnNext is used, for example:
                                       •   To check operator inputs after clicking the "Next" key
                                       •   To return to the input
                                       At this point in time, set values of the dialog page are checked by exporting system
                                       variables.
                                       You can interrupt the dialog execution in the script by applying the "Redo()
                                       (Page 121)" procedure. In this case, you can correct settings of the dialog page.
                                       You can restart execution of the dialog page. The "OnNext" script is also executed
                                       again.
                   OnEnd (Page 257) After processing has been completed, the script is executed at the end of a dialog
                                    page.
                                       Through write access to system variables you set which of the following dialogs are
                                       to be executed or not executed.

8.5.5.2        Inserting and editing scripts


Add new script
                  1. Select the event for which you want to create a script.
                  2. In the Project explorer toolbar (Page 227), select "Add script" > "Create new script".


Link an existing script
                  1. Select the event into which you want to link a script.
                  2. In the Project explorer toolbar (Page 227), select "Add script" > "Link existing script".
                  3. In the open window, navigate to the required script file (*.upscr).
                  4. Confirm with "Open".
                     The script you selected will be linked and added to the selected event.


Edit dialog scripts
                  You edit the dialog scripts in the "Script Editor", which is integrated in CMC Expert.
                  Open the "Script Editor" in CMC Expert by double clicking on the desired script.
                  The script is opened in a new tab in the working area. You can edit new as well as linked
                  scripts.
                  You insert CMC scripts via the "Insert script" shortcut menu.

                                              If you are not completely certain that the package will be handled in a
                                              responsible fashion, do not save any password in the package.
                                              You are solely responsible for saving the passwords in the package.

Backup SD card

                   Execute backup          You select a data backup of the NCU/PPU on this dialog page at the start of
                                           package execution.
                                           The content of the SD card, including the current active archive data (NC, PLC,
                                           DRV) is backed up in a folder named after the SD card ID.
                                           If a data backup is found next to the package when starting, you can select this
                                           data backup in the package selection for restoration.
                                           When the backup is restored, the backed-up archive data is reloaded auto‐
                                           matically.
                                           In addition to the data backup "*.tgz", this folder also contains instructions
                                           "*.txt" and a package "*.usz" for a Linux package or "*.exe" for a Windows
                                           package, for restoring the data backup.
                                           A confirmation prompt appears if a backup not belonging to this SD card ID is
                                           to be restored.
                                           You can find more information in the section "Package execution (Page 407)".
                                           To activate the function, click the check box.
                   Setting                 Locked
                                           During package execution, operators can only view the settings made when
                                           configuring; however, these can no longer be changed.


                  Note
                  For "Setting locked" property
                  The setting for selecting the data backup can be locked for the operating procedure.
                  The licenses of the control are also backed up. When restoring a backup, a query appears as to
                  whether the licenses from the backup are to be restored, or the licenses on the control are to be
                  retained.




Archive

                   Back up archive    You can also create a complete archive for the diagnostics, with the setting that all
                                      data is to be backed up.

                                      with the name "Origin_<Date>.dsf".
                   Archive areas      Specify the archive areas that you wish to back up.
                                      You can specifically exclude archive areas from the archive backup. This option can
                                      only be recommended if the backup of an archive area has a significant negative
                                      impact on the performance, and is not relevant from the application perspective.
                   Setting            Locked
                                      During package execution, operators can only view the settings made when con‐
                                      figuring; however, these can no longer be changed.

Installing SINUMERIK Operate on a PCU
                     As of CMC Expert V6.3, it is possible to install SINUMERIK Operate on a PCU. The following must
                     be observed:
                     • CMC supports only synchronous setups on a PCU. During the setup, it does not return control
                       to CMC Shield.
                     • Programs that execute their setups asynchronously by default must be parameterized or
                       wrapped accordingly. Otherwise, an automatic setup is not possible.


Example CNC software setup on a PCU




                     Copy the installation files to "c:\Install\".




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                      287
Create MyConfig - Expert
8.5 Dialogs


                  It is important that the setup of the SINUMERIK Operate is performed synchronously. This
                  requires a specially parameterized command.




                  cmd.exe /c start /wait c:\Install\IPC\SINUMERIK_OPERATE_ipc.exe /
                  clone_wait /s /v"/qb-! DOTNET=1"
                  A reboot is required after the setup.




                  The content of the called file for the reboot looks like this:
                  cmd /c shutdown /r
                  Do not use "shutdown /r -t0", because in this case CMC Shield has no more time to save its
                  status information.

Installation

                      Mode                   •   None
                                                 The software is not installed.
                                             •   New installation
                                                 The SD card is deleted and the system software is reinstalled.
                                                 A memory reset is performed for the NC subsystems and the default data is
                                                 loaded.
                                             •   Upgrade
                                                 The CNC software is replaced by the specified SINUMERIK software version.
                                                 During the upgrade, the user data is migrated.
                                                 Note
                                                 Data migration means that the backed-up archive is imported from the previous
                                                 firmware version to the newly installed firmware version.
                                                 The step execution is performed later based on the archive data of the newly
                                                 installed firmware version.
                                             •   Only additional software
                                                 Only the listed additional "*.tgz" packages without CNC software installation or
                                                 upgrade are installed.
                                                 Only elements from the list of "Additional software (*.tgz)" are taken into con‐
                                                 sideration.
                      Setting                Locked
                                             During package execution, operators can still view the "Mode" setting made when
                                             configuring; however, it cannot be changed.

8.5 Dialogs


DRV archive data/drive configuration
                  In the "DRV archive data/drive configuration" property group, you can specify via the "Origin of
                  data" property whether drive commissioning will be performed in the production step by
                  "Automatic configuration" or "User-specified topology".

Origin of data       •     "Initial state"
                           Data is not reset when upgrading the CNC software. The archive is used that is available in the
                           system after data migration.
                           For a new installation of the CNC software, an empty DRV archive is created.
                     •     "Automatic configuration"
                           The "Automatic configuration" selection runs through the drive unit configuration during the pack‐
                           age execution in the same way as SINUMERIK Operate.
                           "Automatic configuration" mode initially restores the SINAMICS factory settings.
                           Then, automatic HMI device configuration (including DO sorting, BICO interconnection, etc.) takes
                           place.
                           You work with a "comparison topology (*.ust)", which is inserted in the "SINAMICS topology" dialog
                           page. This means that the automatically identified SINAMICS target topology can be compared
                           with a comparison topology generated offline.
                           During "Automatic configuration", SINAMICS determines the target topology, which includes all
                           modules connected at this time, including their DRIVE-CLiQ wiring.
                           In the subsequent package execution, the most recently created online archive is always used. It is
                           only possible to change the topology by adding, removing or replacing components via SINUMER‐
                           IK Operate. Or you must perform a configuration again.
                           Note
                           First encoder on the CU or downstream of the HUB
                           If during a drive data generation via "Automatic configuration" a first encoder (SMI or SMC) is
                           connected downstream of a HUB or to the CU, then a complete automatic configuration of the drive
                           by SINAMICS and CMC Shield is not possible.
                           Parameter "P1982" (Pole position identification on) is set to "1" by SINAMICS instead of "0" and
                           cannot be corrected automatically here.
                           The user can correct the parameter manually or also in the step tree of a CMC package. Set pa‐
                           rameter "P1982=0" in the step tree in a component for all drives whose first encoder is connected
                           downstream of the HUB or to the CU.
                     •     "User-specified topology"
                           With the selection "user-specified topology", a user-specified topology (*.utz2) is loaded during
                           package execution.
                           For drive commissioning, a user-specified topology can be loaded that also contains modules that
                           will not be added, wired and activated until later during commissioning.
                           The necessary data objects are created by SINAMICS, also for the modules that are not yet present,
                           so that the user data can already be loaded during package execution.
                           In the subsequent package execution, the most recently created online archive is always used.
                           A main application case for this are DQI/SMI motors and encoders. The Cu and the NX expansion
                           modules must always be present.
                           The user-specified topology (*.utz2) is specified in dialog "SINAMICS topology".
                     •     "Offline archive"
                           The data from a SINUMERIK archive are used.
                     •     "Do not use"
                           The dialog page does not provide any initial data for this area. Data of the area is also not transferred
                           to the control.
                           More information can be found in Section "Archive data transfer (package execution) (Page 319)".

Axis-drive assignment
                   An automatic Axis-drive assignment is only realized in variants "Comparison topology" and "User-
                   specified topology", as only these variants use the appropriate configuration from CMC Topo.
                   As a prerequisite, this Axis-drive assignment must have been configured and activated in
                   CMC Topo for the comparison or User-specified topology.
                   By activation, with equal rights, of the Axis-drive assignment in CMC Topo, there is a
                   guarantee that not only the expert for CMC Expert, but also the expert for CMC Topo will
                   agree to this assignment.
                   Moreover, it is possible for the project engineer for CMC Expert and the operator during
                   package execution to deactivate the automatic Axis-drive assignment without having to open
                   and edit the topology files.
                   The following properties available for the "axis-drive assignment" are activated during
                   package execution:

                    Activation         Specify whether you want to activate the automatic "axis-drive assignment".
                    Setting            Locked
                                       During package execution, operators can only view the settings made when con‐
                                       figuring; however, these can no longer be changed.

                      List                   Using button , open window "List (Comparison topology (*.ust))" with the fol‐

                     drive objects for modules that are still not available.

                     configured for the drives during system configuration (configuration):
                     • Initial state
                     • Offline archive

8.5.31           Step tree (configuration)
                     This dialog allows you to create an archive before and after executing the step tree.




                     Figure 8-55     Step tree - project engineer view



Basic dialog settings
                     Information can be found in the section "Basic dialog settings (Page 252)".
                     Information on the system variables for this dialog can be found in the section "System
                     variables for the Step tree dialog (Page 382)".


Archive
                     The settings for the creation of archives before and after execution of the step tree are specified
                     by the project engineer. Settings are not displayed during package execution.
                     An archive with the NC, DRV, HMI and SYS areas is created. The backup is performed for the
                     NC area with the setting that all data is to be saved.
                     You can use the archives for the diagnostics. The archives are not required for the production
                     or the upgrade of a machine.
                     The archive always includes archive areas available at the event instant, independent of how
                     the actual use is configured.
                     The archive is stored in the folder named after the "SD card ID" which is located next to the
                     package after the package execution.
                     If no NCU is involved with the package execution, the archive is stored in the "SD-NoneNCU"
                     folder.

                      Create before the step     If you activate the check box, an archive is created before the step tree has
                      tree                       been executed.
                                                 The archive is backed up with the name StepBegin_<Date>.dsf.
                      Create after the step tree If you activate the check box, an archive is created after the step tree has been
                                                 executed.
                                                 The archive is backed up with the name "StepEnd_<Date>.dsf".
                      Without HMI share          If you activate the check box, the archive is created before or after the step tree
                                                 without the HMI part.

8.5.33           Archive data transfer (package execution)
                     While this dialog page is being displayed, the manipulated archive data of NC, DRV, HMI and SYS
                     is transferred to the controller.
                     The "Archive data transfer" is not listed in CMC Expert because the dialog, without having
                     to be configured, is automatically called from the package if the package data is transferred
                     from at least one of the areas NC, DRV, HMI or SYS to the controller.
                     The archive data of the folders NC, DRV, HMI and SYS have their source corresponding
                     to what has been configured on dialog page "System configuration" and are possibly
                     manipulated, removed or added by the package.
                     All archive data, which is available at the end of dialog page "Step tree" is transferred to the
                     control.
                     Operations carried out on archive data in scripts and actions in dialogs after the "Step tree"
                     are no longer active.

                  This applies to:
                  • Copying, deleting and manipulating files in the archive area
                  • Manipulating machine data
                  • Manipulating drive data
                  • Scripts with file operations in the archive area
                  Still possible after the "Step tree":
                  • Operations that directly access the NCU/IPC
                     – Copying, deleting and manipulating files in the NCU/PCU/Operate area
                     – Actions of type "Execute"
                  • Scripts without archive manipulation
                     – Controlling the sequence
                     – File operations without archive area


                  Note
                  System variable for the "Origin of data"
                  It is not permissible that the system variable for "Origin of data" is set to "Do not use" in dialog
                  "System configuration", as otherwise archive data is not transferred to the control.

8.6 Steps


8.6            Steps


8.6.1          Overview


Structuring of the steps
                  In the step tree, you can model the different machine variants that belong to a series.
                  You can create the various machine variants by structuring the steps in several levels - in
                  main steps and substeps. You can activate or deactivate individual steps in the step tree.
                  Properties are defined for each step during configuration. You can configure the control
                  elements to activate the steps for the "m" out of "n" selection. If the step is not configured as
                  "Locked", then the operator can change the specified step activations at the machine during
                  package execution.


Package execution
                  For package execution, the step tree is executed from top to bottom.
                  A step is executed when the check box of a step is activated and all higher-level steps, which
                  lead to the substep, are also activated.
                  You can see whether a step is actually being executed in the step properties under the "Step
                  configuration", Property "Execute".
                  When creating the step tree, arrange the steps in the sequence they should be in during
                  package execution.




8.6.2          Step tree structure


Step tree structure
                  The step tree has a hierarchical structure encompassing:
                  • Steps and substeps
                  • Scripts (Page 342)
                  • Actions (Page 348)




                                                                                       Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
338                                                                         Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                 Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                                   8.6 Steps




                                                                        Colors
                                                                        Linked elements are shown in blue.
                                                                        Invalid links are shown in red.




                     Example structure of a step tree

                     You can insert, link or remove steps via the toolbar in the Project explorer (Page 227). The
                     step tree can also be edited via the context menu or using keyboard shortcuts (Page 230).
                     The step numbering has no functional significance, and is used to improve the overall
                     orientation.
                     The step name can be freely selected. The ID of the step is in square brackets after the name.
                     You can expand and collapse the view in the step tree using the toolbar in the Project
                     explorer. The toolbar also provides a preview of the step tree during package processing.
                     You define the visibility of actions and scripts in the Settings (Page 225).


Status indicator of the steps

                                  The step is activated, and is executed during package execution.
                                  The step is activated and is not executed during package execution.
                                  The step is not activated and is executed during package execution.
                                  The step is blocked during package execution and cannot be activated or deactivated by the
                                  operator.

8.6.6          Linking steps


8.6.6.1        Overview
                  Steps from other projects can be linked in a target project. The linked steps can contain any
                  number of substeps, scripts and actions.
                  There are 2 options for linking steps:
                  • Dynamic - linking a step from another project
                    When updating the source project, the linked content is also updated
                  • Static - linking step from a step project
                    A step project is part of a step tree that is exported externally so that it can be linked to one
                    or several projects. The content can no longer be changed after export.
                  Linked steps include attributes (Page 348) from the source project. You can change the
                  attributes in the target project. This means that changed attributes become local attributes,
                  which are independent of the source project.

                  Linked steps have the following advantages:
                  • The configuration engineer creates the subtree once
                  • Central archiving and management
                  • Centralized provision, independent of a CMC project
                  • Multiple use for recurring step sequences


8.6.6.2        Export step as step project
                  When commissioning machines, sometimes several projects must be managed.




                                                                                           Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
344                                                                             Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                              8.6 Steps


                     To support users, a subtree can be exported from a step tree. This subtree, designated as
                     "Step project", is externally archived from a CMC Expert project. Customers create the step
                     project, and this is managed at a central location.


Procedure
                     In a step tree of a CMC Expert project, you have created a step with substeps, scripts and actions.
                     You require this subtree in this or other projects for step sequences that are being continually
                     used. To simplify the procedure, export this part of the step tree as autonomous step project.
                     1. In the Project explorer, select the step from which you wish to export the step project.
                     2. In the step project toolbar (Page 340), click on the "Export step as step project" button.



                     3. Navigate to the target folder.
                        You can already create and name the target directory on any drive beforehand.
                        Note:
                        The target folder for the step project must not contain any other data. Only one empty folder
                        or one folder with an existing step project is permissible. An existing step project will be
                        replaced.
                        Folders containing other files are not emptied.
                     4. Specify the file name (*.upstep) and save the step project.
                        – Links with resolution at package creation
                          The links are resolved when exporting, and the data are transferred to the step project.
                        – Links with resolution at runtime
                          The links are accepted, and are only resolved during the package runtime.
                     You can also export a step project via the command line mode (Page 404).


8.6.6.3          Link step
                     A linked step also includes attributes from the source project. You can change the attributes in
                     the target project. This means that changed attributes become local attributes, which are
                     independent of the source project.

                     1. Select the position in the step tree.
                     2. In the Project explorer toolbar (Page 228), click on button "Link step from another project".




                        If you wish to link the step as substep, click on button "Link substeps from other project".
                     3. Specify the file type.
                        If you wish to link to a step in another CMC Expert project, then select data type *.upproj.
                        If you want to link to a step project, then select file type *.upstep.
                     4. Navigate to the corresponding folder.

Properties of the linked step
                     A step or a step project can be integrated into a CMC Expert project at several locations.
                     Only properties marked with the attribute "From external step project" can be changed in the
                     linked step.



                     If an attribute in the linked step is changed, then the change is applicable for the modified
                     location. As a consequence, the changed value replaces the value from the external source
                     project at the current location, and deletes attribute "From external step project". This means
                     that future changes in the external source project are no longer updated for this changed
                     property as a local definition exists for the property.

                     The step can only be deleted from the project as complete subtree. The attributes that you

                     In the case of a new link, you must adapt the local attributes that you require.


Procedure
                     1. Select the linked step.
                     2. In the Project explorer toolbar (Page 228), click on button "Remove from project tree".




                        The linked step is deleted.
                     3. Save the project.

8.6.6.6        Import step attributes from step project
                  The attributes from the external source project that can be edited can be transferred to the linked
                  step in the CMC Expert project. Attributes already existing in the project are overwritten by the
                  external source project. From this point in time, this data is part of the project and can be freely
                  modified.
                  Updating the source project no longer changes these attributes. When updating, the
                  attributes of new steps in the source project are shown as linked attributes just the same
                  as for the linking ("From external step project").
                  To also accept these attributes in the project, initiate a new import of the step attributes,
                  therefore overwriting local deviations. Or you must manually edit the attributes of the new
                  steps, therefore overwriting them.


Procedure
                  1. Select the linked step.
                  2. In the step project toolbar (Page 340), click on the "Import step attributes from the step
                     project" button.



                     The linked step is assigned the attributes from the external source project.
                     All of the changed local attributes are overwritten, and reassigned the attributes from the
                     external source project.




8.7            Actions


8.7.1          Actions in the package execution
                  In order for an action to be executed during package execution, an action must be linked to a step
                  and the step must be activated for execution An action script can permit or prevent execution of
                  the action.
                  An action is configured, for example, by creating instructions in the action script, creating
                  and editing new tasks, and linking required tasks and/or files.



                                                                                        Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
348                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                            Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                             8.7 Actions


                     Every action is opened in a separate tab. The tab also includes an action script, which you
                     can populate with your instructions. Folders and new tasks can be created and new files
                     linked.
                     During package execution, the actions are executed from top to bottom in the sequence of
                     the listing in the step tree depending on the steps. An action is activated when the step
                     linked to the action is activated.
                     All the relevant instructions and data are inserted in the respective action under the relevant
                     tab during the configuration.

                     Note
                     Sequence and execution of actions in the step tree
                     The sequence of the steps in the step tree is relevant for the sequence and execution of the
                     actions. The actions are assigned to the steps respectively. Actions are processed in the order
                     below a step.

                     Note
                     Changes becoming effective through actions
                     If data in the archive area (DSF archive) is changed by actions, this change only becomes
                     effective after the step tree has been processed by the archive data transfer (Page 319).
                     Changes through actions outside the DSF archive take effect in the respective target area
                     immediately with the respective action. However, these changes can be overwritten again by an
                     archive data transfer following the step tree.

8.7.4            Editing actions


Creating an action
                     An action is always created below a step, and is therefore automatically assigned to this step.
                     Actions can be created via the toolbar of the Project explorer or via the context menu.
                     1. Select the step for which you want to create an action.
                     2. Click the "Add action" button in the Project explorer toolbar and select the desired action.
                        The action is created and linked with the step.


                     Note

                     As of CMC V6.7, you can recognize the type of action by the icon for newly created actions. The
                     old icon is still displayed for actions that were created with earlier CMC versions. The icon is only
                     updated after an action has been opened.

                     commenting.

                     variables for "Modify".

                     If folders, files, sections or identifiers are not available, then the package itself generates these
                     to implement a value assignment.

                      =         Assignment of a new value
                      ~         Delete date: Identifier and value are removed
                      ?=        Assigning a (new) value if no value is available

8.7 Actions


Create delete task
                  1. Open the action and select the folder in the target area.
                  2. Create a new file or file link via the Toolbar actions (Page 356).
                     – "New file": You can freely select task names.
                     – "Link new file": The task name is assigned the file name of the linked file. You can rename
                       the task via the toolbar.
                     The file or file link can be opened and edited using the integrated "Script Editor".
                  If required, you can divide the delete instructions into several tasks to improve the structure.
                  When executing, the files specified in the tasks are deleted without any prior confirmation
                  prompt.


Notes regarding file and folder names
                  The names of the files and folders to be deleted are specified in the "Delete instructions".
                  The following wildcards are permitted in the file names:
                  • "*" - for none or one or several arbitrary characters
                  • "?" - one arbitrary character
                  On the other hand, no place holders are permitted in the folder names. Folders are deleted
                  with their complete content.
                  Only one delete operation is permissible for each line.
                  If a line starts with a comment character ";", then the line is not evaluated.

                  Examples:

                  Cycle*.spf         All cycles in the current folder are deleted.
                  *.*                All files in the current folder are deleted; subfolders are kept.
                  4711.WPD           Folder 4711.WPD with all of its contents is deleted.

                  Note
                  Case sensitivity on the NCU/PPU
                  In contrast to Microsoft Windows, the file system used on the NCU/PPU differentiates between
                  upper case and lower case letters.

8.7.11           "Execute" action


8.7.11.1         Description of "Execute" action


Execute action
                     The "Execute" action allows a program, command or script to be executed. For example, you can
                     install software components from SIEMENS or other suppliers - or perform special
                     manipulations in the archive or other target areas (Page 349).


Target areas

                     Table 8-19     Target areas "Execute" action

                      Target area            Description                          Example
                      NCU                    Root of the NCU/PPU                  -
                      PCU                    PCU drives/shares                    -
                      Linux                  Runtime system                       -
                      Windows                                                     -



Execute, general
                     Enter all the files and folders required for "Execute" as link under the appropriate target area.
                     When the package is created, the links are resolved and the folders and files are accepted in the
                     package.
                     You can specify a command or an executable file in the "Execution of:" field. You can also pass
                     arguments separated by spaces, e.g. file names, switches.
                     Write commands or file names that contain spaces in straight quotation marks.
                     Special operators (Page 68) can be inserted anywhere in the field.
                     During execution, all folders and files are unzipped into a temporary folder. This temporary
                     folder is used as work directory when "executing" and is then deleted.

                     Note
                     Temporary folder
                     The temporary folder is not the package storage. This means a "./" used for "Execution of:"
                     does not point next to the package but to the temporary folder.




Execute - NCU
                     The script outputs are transferred to the logbook. In this case, the error messages (stderr) of the
                     programs called in the script are entered in italics.

                  The return value of the script is evaluated as terminating error code. A return code not equal
                  to "0" results in an error message. The user must decide whether the package should be
                  canceled or continued.
                  More information is provided in Section "Notes regarding executing an action (Page 370)".


Execute - PCU
                  For an installation, additional operator actions may be required on the PCU.

                  Examples of "Execution of"

                           Setup.exe -OF:opfile.sl
                           Cmd.exe /c"mein start.cmd"

                  The return value of the script is evaluated as terminating error code. A return code not equal

Execute - Runtime system
                     A package can be created for various runtime systems.
                     In order to be able to deploy a package that makes changes via "Execute" for both Linux and
                     Microsoft Windows, it is necessary to write 2 scripts.
                     Depending on the runtime system, Windows or Linux, the corresponding node is executed
                     automatically and the other skipped during execution.
                     The script outputs are transferred to the logbook. In this case, the error messages (stderr) of
                     the programs called in the script are entered in italics.
                     The return value of the script is evaluated as terminating error code. A return code not equal
                     to "0" results in an error message. The user must decide whether the package should be
                     canceled or continued.

                     Example
                     All files, except for "OEM001.SPF", should be deleted from folder CMA.DIR of the NC.
                     As there is no special delete instruction for this purpose, a script is generated which saves the
                     file to be obtained, subsequently deletes the folder and then returns the file.
                     The particular script file is copied to the component and entered as a command for "Execute".

                     Microsoft Windows
                         Md .\Save
                         Move %UP_ARC%\NC\NCU_<name>\NCK\cycles\cma.dir\OEM001.SPF .\Save\
                         Del /Q %UP_ARC%\NC\NCU_<name>\NCK\cycles\cma.dir\*.*
                         Move .\Save\OEM001.SPF %UP_ARC%\NC\NCU_<name>\NCK\cycles\cma.dir\
                     Linux
                         mkdir ./Save
                         mv $UP_ARC/NC/NCU_<name>/NCK/cycles/cma.dir/OEM001.SPF ./Save/
                         rm -r $UP_ARC/NC/NCU_<name>/NCK/cycles/cma.dir/*
                         mv ./Save/OEM001.SPF $UP_ARC/NC/NCU_<name>/NCK/cycles/cma.dir/

8.7 Actions


8.7.11.2       "Notes relating to the Execute action"

                  Note
                  System variables for the environment
                  Use "System variables for the environment" in a script file for Microsoft Windows "cmd" or Linux
                  "sh", because only these script files are known to the script interpreter.
                  If, however, "System variables for the environment" are used in "Execution of" the component,
                  for Linux use a "sh" as prefix, and for Microsoft Windows, a "cmd" as prefix before the command.
                  The "System variables for the environment" can be used in all CMC scripts.
                  Example:
                  If !FileExist(RTS,"%UP_PACK%/WCD/File.txt")
                  As alternative to UP_PACK, the system variable Up.$Pack.Dir can also be used for "Execution
                  of" and in all CMC scripts.
                  Example:
                  md "$(Up.$Pack.Dir)/WCD"
                  If !FileExist(RTS,"$(Up.$Pack.Dir)/WCD/File.txt")
                  System variables for the environment
                  UP_PACK - Location from where the package was started
                  UP_ARC - Temporary storage location of the archive tree with subfolders
                  UP_SDID - ID of the SD card
                  UP_PCU_ROOT - Computer name of the "PCU".
                  Available only for packages with the "PCU" data area.
                  UP_ARC_ROOT - Folder of the archives to be processed.
                  Available only for packages that use only the "Use archive" data area.

                  Note
                  Exit Script
                  If no script-internal error handling is performed, a script should preferably always be exited with
                  exit "0".

                  Note
                  Command interpreter under Microsoft Windows
                  For Microsoft Windows, prefix the command line scripts to the command interpreter.
                  For example:
                  Cmd.exe /c test.cmd




                                                                                       Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
370                                                                         Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                           8.7 Actions


                     Note
                     Using shell scripts for Linux
                     When using shell scripts "*.sh" for Linux, always ensure that in the Unix file format you only
                     save LF; and not CR/LF.
                     The shell identifier must be located in the first line, e.g.:
                     #!/bin/sh
                     The script must be started using a shell call, e.g.:
                     sh my_script.sh
                     If you specify commands directly with place holders or environment variables, then use a shell as
                     prefix e.g.:
                     sh rm /user/*.log.
                     If you specify a file for execution, then use "./" as prefix, e.g.:
                     ./test.sh.




8.7.12           Creating a file link (resolution during runtime)

                     Note
                     Runtime links
                     When using runtime links, you must ensure that only the required files are linked in.
                     Unintentional or malicious modification of these files may result in unexpected or harmful
                     response when processing packets




Requirement
                     • The action is open.
                     • The folder is created in the target area.

                     1. Select the folder in the target area in which you wish to create the file link.
                     2. In the Actions toolbar (Page 356), click on button "Create new file link (resolution at
                        runtime)".



                     3. Enter the name of the file. When executing the package, the file is saved to the target system.

Create MyConfig - Expert
8.7 Actions


                  4. Directly enter the link path to the source file or select it from the     button.
                  5. Confirm with "OK".
                     The path is resolved at runtime.
                     The link path must be valid at the time that the package is executed.




                  More information on marking files in actions (Page 351).




8.7.13         Creating a folder link (resolution during runtime)

                  Note
                  Runtime links
                  When using runtime links, you must ensure that only the required files are linked in.
                  Unintentional or malicious modification of these files may result in unexpected or harmful
                  response when processing packets




Requirement
                  • The action is open.
                  • The folder is created in the target area.


Procedure
                  1. Select the folder in the target area that you wish to link with another folder on the target
                     system.
                  2. In the Actions toolbar (Page 356), click on button "Create new folder link (resolution at
                     runtime)".



                  3. Enter the name of the folder. When executing the package, the folder is created on the target
                     system, assuming that it was not available.


                                                                                        Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
372                                                                          Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                  8.9 Reference list, system variables


                     4. Directly enter the link path to the source folder or select it from the   button.
                     5. Confirm with "OK".
                        The path is resolved at runtime.
                        The link path must be valid at the time that the package is executed.




                     The linked folder is displayed purple in the target area (Page 349).

8.9              Reference list, system variables


8.9.1            General information about system variables


System variables for CMC Expert
                     You use system variables in scripts and during configuration. System variables depend on
                     the dialogs (Page 249), therefore you call the system variables directly in the dialog.
                     Most system variables are provided with values for the first time during configuration. These
                     values can be modified when using configuration files to create and/or execute the package.
                     Some variables are only available during the package execution.
                     Also during the package execution, you can change system variables in dialog scripts or
                     change tasks by write access operations before these system variables become active in the
                     sequence.

                   Conventions
                   Take the following conventions into account:
                   • Upper/lower case is not relevant.
                   • For compound names, the beginnings of words are written in uppercase to improve legibility
                   • Values of enumerations are written in uppercase throughout

8.9.7.3          Activate step


Activate step - Up.$Step[id].Activated
                     The activation status of a specific step is defined in the step tree using the
                     "Up.$Step[id].Activated" system variable.
                     System variable "Up.$Step[id].Activated" supplies value "true" for all steps, whose
                     check box "Activate step" has a check mark.
                     The value "false" is supplied for all steps that are not activated.
                     After a step is activated, the "Execute" property is automatically activated in the "Step
                     configuration" property group.
                     Whether the step is actually executed or not depends on the upstream steps. The substep is
                     not executed if a substep is activated, however the higher-level main step is not activated.
                     You configure the "Step configuration" for each step individually via the check box, which you
                     can then activate or deactivate again.

                     Note
                     Step activation
                     You can also configure step activation directly in the step tree. The step activation becomes
                     immediately active.




See also
                     Step properties (Page 340)


8.9.7.4          Lock step activation


Step activation locked - Up.$Step[id].Locked
                     The activation status of a step is locked for package execution with the
                     "Up.$Step[id].Locked" system variable.

                   System variable "Up.$Step[id].Locked"supplies value "true" for all steps, whose check box
                   "Locked" has a check mark.

                   Note
                   Main step locked
                   If you remove the lock from the main step, the substeps will remain locked.
                   The locking of a substep must be undone for each individual step.

8.9.7.5         Collapse step


Collapsing steps - Up.$Step[id].Collapsed
                   The selected step is shown collapsed in the step tree with the "Up.$Step[id].Collapsed"
                   system variable. The operator cannot see the step.
                   System variable "Up.$Step[id].Collapsed" returns value "true" for all steps whose check
                   box for "Collapsed" is activated.

                   Note
                   Collapse steps
                   The "Collapsed" status only becomes effective during package execution. The user cannot have
                   these steps displayed.




See also
                   Step properties (Page 340)

8.10             Create package
                       For Microsoft Windows and Linux systems, you can create Create MyConfig packages using
                       CMC Expert.
                       For Linux operating systems running on the NCU/PPU, CMC Expert generates a file with the
                       extension "*.usz" (Linux package).
                       For Microsoft Windows operating systems running on the IPC, PG or PC, a file with the
                       extension "*.exe" (Windows package) is generated.
                       These packages are then executed under the respective operating system. You configure the
                       runtime system settings in the "Configuration (Page 237)".

Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                           393
Create MyConfig - Expert
8.11 Command line call


Notes

                  Note
                  Specification of the complete path of "ExpertCmd.exe"
                  Specify the complete path of the "ExpertCmd.exe", or include the path in the environment
                  variable "Path".
                  Example:
                  "C:\Program Files\Siemens\Automation\SINUMERIK\Create MyConfig 6.10\ExpertCmd.exe"

                  Note
                  Path data
                  • Set the specified paths in straight quotation marks if spaces are included.
                     Example:
                     "C:\path with spaces\Expert_Logfile.xml"
                  • When specifying folders, path data may only end with '\', e.g. -d "D:\packages\"
                  • The file name extensions are not added automatically and must be specified in the path.

                  Note
                  Saving batch files
                  Always save batch files with ANSI/ASCII encoding.

                  Note
                  Umlauts and special characters
                  Avoid the use of umlauts and special characters in path names.
                  To allow special characters or umlauts to be correctly processed in specified paths, save the batch
                  files with command line calls with the same character set as used by the region-specific
                  command line interpreter "cmd.exe".
                  For example, "Codepage 850", also known as "DOS-Latin-1", applies to the region Western
                  Europe.
                  The "Notepad" editor integrated in Microsoft Windows does not support saving files with this
                  character set.

                  Note
                  Uppercase/lowercase
                  For command line parameters, always use the specified uppercase/lowercase notation.

                     The relative path with ".\" or "./" refers to the current work folder, where the batch or CMD

                     If no path is specified, the work folder is used.
