8.11.6         Creating files with encrypted information


gensecfiles
                  The gensecfiles command is used to read passwords from an input file in XML format and save
                  them in encrypted form in new password files.
                  The input file contains the password and the associated file name and path for output. A
                  password file is created for each password file.
                  The password file with the encrypted PLC access level password is saved with the file name
                  extension uppal.
                  The password file with the encrypted password for the PLC configuration data is saved with
                  the file name extension uppms.
                  The authentication files with the encrypted access data for the respective access level of the
                  SINUMERIK Operate are saved with the file name extension upauth.




                                                                                      Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
400                                                                        Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                               Create MyConfig - Expert
                                                                                                8.11 Command line call


                     The password file with the encrypted password for the security archive is saved with the file
                     name extension upsapwd.
                     The authentication files with the encrypted access data for UMC login are saved with file
                     name extension upauth.
                     Password rules in Create MyConfig (Page 472)

                     Call
                     ExpertCmd.exe gensecfiles [options] <secdatainput>
                     Write the command and all parameters used in one line. Observe the notes on the command
                     line call (Page 393).
                     Information on errors and warnings can be found in section "Return values (Page 406)".


Parameter

                      Argument       Required/    Description
                                     optional
                      secdatainput   Required     Input file with plain text information in XML format
                                                  The input file can contain the following passwords:
                                                  •   PLC access level password
                                                  •   Password for PLC configuration data
                                                  •   SINUMERIK access level passwords
                                                  •   Security archive password
                                                  •   Access data for UMC login



                      Option         Required/    Description
                                     optional
                      -h             Optional     Information on the command line parameters
                      --help
                      -o             Optional     An existing file will be overwritten.
                      --overwrite



Encryption method
                     The encryption method corresponds to the Protection class for password information
                     (Page 240) in the security settings.
                     The "CMCProd" encryption method stands for the "CMC standard" protection class.
                     For the "TransportPWD" encryption method, the password is specified in the
                     transportpwdtouse attribute.

<CMCSecurityDataGeneration xmlns="http://Siemens.com/DI/
XMLSchema_CMCSecurityDataGeneration.xsd" version="1.1">

  <!-- no functionality connected -->
  <Target name="Machine 1" date="2023-12-15 18:23:42">

      <!-- CMC V6.7, only method="CMCProd" allowed -->
      <Encryption method="CMCProd" >
      </Encryption>

      <!--        <TransportPWD transportpwdtouse="12345678"/> -->
      <!-- <Encryption/> -->
    </Control>

         <!-- password: password to encode in cleartext -->
         <!-- file: requested output file path and name, relative to the current location --
>
         <!--            extension upauth will be added automatically -->
         <PAL password="password1" file ="subdir\myuppal.uppal" />

        <!-- not used in CMC V6.7 -->
        <HMI>
          <AuthDataClassic>
            <!-- username: constant value: "manufact" | "service" | "user"-->
            <!-- password: password to encode in cleartext -->
            <!-- file: requested output file path and name, relative to the current location
-->
             <!--       extension upauth will be added automatically -->

                          file = "...any_name_for_manufact_pwd_file..."/>
             <AccessLevel username="service" password="...clearTextPwd..."
                          file = "...any_name_for_service_pwd_file..."/>
             <AccessLevel username="user" password="...clearTextPwd..."
                          file = "...any_name_for_user_pwd_file..."/>
           </AuthDataClassic>
           <SecArchPassword>
             <!-- password: password to encode in cleartext -->
             <!-- file: requested output file path and name, relative to the current location
-->
             <!--       extension upsapwd will be added automatically -->
             <SecArch password="...clearTextPwd..." file = "...any_name_for_pwd_file..." />
           </SecArchPassword>
           <AuthDataUMCLocal>
             <!-- domain: the domain the user belongs to -->
             <!-- username: cleartext -->
             <!-- password: password to encode in cleartext -->
             <!-- file: requested output file path and name, relative to the current location
-->
              <!--       extension upauth will be added automatically -->
              <UMC domain="OEM" username="any clear text data" password="...clearTextPwd..."

9.1 Package execution


9.1.2          Requirements


Package execution using NCU/PPU
                  Observe the following points if an NCU/PPU is involved during package execution (NCU/PPU data
                  area active):
                  • To prevent errors during package execution, the NCU/PPU system state must be consistent.
                  • Before starting a CMC package, the NCU/PPU must be in the following state:
                        – LEDs "RDY" and "RUN" are lit green
                        – The 7-segment display indicates a "6" with flashing point
                  • If system software is on the SD card, then the following must apply before starting a package:
                        – The NC status display is at "6"
                        – The PLC status display is "green".
                        Use a service stick for an SD card without system software.
                  • Load the factory settings prior to a drive unit configuration if inconsistent data is found on the
                    control. Failure to adhere to this can lead to undefined conditions.
                  • For a drive unit configuration - automatic configuration or user-specified topology - carefully
                    ensure that the PLC hardware configuration is consistent with the hardware used regarding
                    the NCU and NX configuration.
                    The PLC hardware configuration may contain more NX modules than are available on the
                    machine.
                  • The SINAMICS data must be consistent and match the hardware configuration.
                  • If you renumber the drive objects, then you are responsible for adapting the BICO
                    interconnections.
                    The BICO interconnections are not adapted automatically by CMC.
                  • On dialog page "End", check that the package was executed without any errors.
                    If processing took place with errors, you must check the log file as to whether there will be
                    any likely effects on functionality.
                  If this state is not present before the start of a CMC commissioning package, then it
                  can be achieved by a memory reset and loading of default data of the individual control
                  components.


Memory reset / load standard data
                  For NCU/PPU, proceed as follows:
                  1. NC: S3 = 1 and OFF/ON.
                  2. Restart the device.
                  3. When running up, wait for the "6" with flashing point. It can take several minutes for the
                     system to run-up.
                  4. Then "S3" back to "0".
                  5. SINAMICS: Empty the folder "user/sinamics/data" on the SD card followed by ON/OFF.

                                                                                           Create MyConfig - packages
                                                                                                 9.1 Package execution


9.1.3            Starting package execution under Microsoft Windows
                     Establish a network connection between the PC and the control devices (NCU 17xx, IPC) that are
                     to be processed with the package.
                     You can start the package created by CMC Expert for Microsoft Windows with the file
                     extension "*.exe" on the IPC, the PG or the PC with "Execute..." or with a double-click.
                     If the package file is the only exe file in the "Install" folder of a USB medium inserted in the IPC
                     (USB FlashDrive, hard disk, CD), then the file is automatically started when the IPC is run-up.

                     Note
                     Simultaneously starting several packages
                     Carefully note that it is not permissible to simultaneously start several packages.
                     A package may only be started if no other package is running.

                     Note
                     Unknown USB medium
                     For existing IPC base systems, ensure that the IPC recognizes the USB medium, as a new medium
                     is installed after the start routine for the package. This means that it may be necessary to insert
                     the USB medium and then switch-off and switch-on the IPC again after
                     approximately 30 seconds.




9.1.4            Package execution dialogs
                     The dialog pages of package execution are described in CMC Expert in the "Dialogs (Page 249)"
                     section.

                     Executing the package under Microsoft Windows
                     Under Microsoft Windows system variables (Page 374) Up.$Pack.DeployName and
                     Up.$Pack.UserVersion are displayed in the title bar when the package is executed. The
                     package name (DeployName) corresponds to the name that was defined in the configuration
                     for generating the package. If you rename the file at a later date, the originally configured
                     package name is displayed in the title bar and not the new file name.

                     Write the command subsequently shown as well as all associated switches and arguments in one
                     line to a batch file or a command line interface.

Notes
                  Note the following information for the command line call:

                  Note
                  Observe the sequence of the switches
                  Write the switches in the specified sequence.
                  Take the sections "Call" and "Parameter" into account.

                  Note
                  Saving batch files
                  Always save batch files with ANSI/ASCII coding.

                  Note
                  Umlauts and special characters
                  Avoid the use of umlauts and special characters in path names.
                  To allow special characters or umlauts to be correctly processed in specified paths, save the batch
                  files with command line calls with the same character set as used by the region-specific
                  command line interpreter "cmd.exe".
                  For example, "Codepage 850", also known as "DOS-Latin-1", applies to the region Western
                  Europe.
                  The "Notepad" editor integrated in Microsoft Windows does not support saving files with this
                  character set.

                  Note
                  Uppercase/lowercase
                  For the command line switches and arguments, always use the specified uppercase/lowercase
                  syntax.

                  Note
                  Absolute/relative path
                  You can specify the absolute path or the relative path.

10.1             Introduction

                     Note
                     Documentation structure: Operating Manual / Online Help
                     Section Create MyConfig Topo has the same layout and structure in the Operating Manual and
                     online help.

                     Note
                     Compatibility with earlier versions
                     • Topo project files
                       Projects saved with CMC Topo V6.10 cannot be opened with previous versions.
                       Projects from previous versions of CMC Topo can be opened with V6.10. When saving the
                       project a message is displayed that the project is no longer compatible with previous versions.
                     • Comparison typology files (UST)
                       UST files, which were exported from CMC Topo V6.10, can no longer be loaded with previous
                       CMC Topo versions.
                     • Command line call
                       Projects and UST files saved with CMC Topo V6.10 run automatically in the silent mode
                       without any conversion messages.


                     The CMC Topo software is used in Create MyConfig to configure, display, print and compare
                     SINAMICS topologies.
                     The following topology variants are available.
                     • Comparison topology
                     • User-specified topology

                     Comparison topology
                     An image of the SINAMICS topology is used for purposes such as:
                     • Check the topology (wiring) of SINAMICS on the machine
                     • Monitor module/component properties
                     • Change module/component names
                     • Change DO numbers and DO names
                     • Assign SINAMICS modules DO variables.
                     SINAMICS modules or components are, for example, Sensor Modules and Motor Modules.

                     User-specified topology
                     Instead of using "Automatic configuration", for SINAMICS, specify an offline (target) topology
                     package (SOT). This device commissioning variant supports a step-by-step production


Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                       413
Create MyConfig - Topo
10.1 Introduction


                    workflow, because modules/components and data that do not physically exist can be
                    configured in the control.


CMC Topo functions
                    • Creating topologies via a graphic user interface
                    • Import of topologies from SINUMERIK archives, from deployed topologies (ECAD XML files)
                    • Import of topologies from Siemens Data Exchange "*.sdx" from EPLAN Add-In
                    • Check run for created topologies
                    • Comparison of topologies
                    • Assignment of module/component properties, e.g. component name, OEM ID.
                    • Specification of criteria (Article No.) that the package compares with the actual properties of
                      the SINAMICS modules on the machine to be produced (read-out TARGET topology of the
                      SINAMICS). Impermissible deviations are reported.
                    • Assignment of the DO variables to modules/components
                    • Creation of a user-specified topology based on generic modules.
                      You can load the user-specified topology directly to SINAMICS when the package is being
                      executed.
                    • Support of a step-by-step commissioning for missing components through deactivation of
                      these components.
                    • A "DOList Editor (Page 432)" is integrated in CMC Topo, which provides effective support
                      when creating DO variables.
                      If you want to edit DO variables "*.uvdx" independent or outside of CMC Topo, then start the
                      "DOList-Editor" via the Microsoft Windows start menu as a single application.


Assignment of DO variables and DO properties
                    You assign DO variables to the modules in CMC Topo. The DO variables provide properties that
                    can be used for configuring the package execution in CMC Expert. You can therefore work
                    flexibly in CMC Expert with defined DO variables, whose absolute values only apply during the
                    package runtime on the machine.
                    You assign SINAMICS modules that do not generate their own DO, to DO-generating modules
                    using DO variables, e.g. "Sensor Module" to "Motor Module".
                    You can therefore save drive-specific parameters in a modular fashion in a package without
                    reference to a particular "DO number", "module number" or "slave".
                    The assignment of the parameters to the topology-specific DO on the machine is controlled
                    flexibly in the scripts using DO variables corresponding to the package configuration.
                    The DRIVE-CLiQ wiring created in CMC Topo and the assignments made for DO variables, DO
                    names and DO numbers are saved via a deploy function to a "*.ust" comparison topology or
                    "*.utz2" user-specified topology.
                    When executing a package, the existing file of the comparison topology or user-specified
                    topology is accessed.

                                                                                                 10.1 Introduction


10.1.1           Network protocol SSH

                     Note
                     Network protocol SSH / archive exchange format DSF
                     To access the NCU or the IPC, programs CMC Shield, CMC Diff and CMC Topo use network
                     protocol "SSH".
                     As standard, the SSH protocol is only available on the NCU as well as Microsoft Windows 10 and
                     Windows 11 systems.
                     Use the archive exchange format "DSF" for exchanging data between other systems/participants.

10.3                 CMC Topo - Operation


10.3.1               Creating a topology
                       CMC Topo offers the option of creating a new topology from the "module catalog". However, you
                       can import and edit a topology from an electrical design system or directly from the control via
                       an archive.
                       The topology can also be displayed from a drive archive, imported, or directly imported from
                       a control and subsequently edited. In this case, the original component numbers and article
                       numbers determined by SINAMICS are entered in the properties of the components. New DO
                       variables are also automatically generated and assigned to the imported components.
                       The DO variables used for CMC commissioning are stored in the control and can be assigned
                       and displayed again.




                                                                                             Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
422                                                                               Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                  Create MyConfig - Topo
                                                                                              10.3 CMC Topo - Operation


                     Representation types Topology tree / Topology graph
                     A topology is represented in 2 ways in CMC Topo.
                     • In a hierarchically structured tree representation
                     • In a systematic, graphic representation
                     Both representation types make it easy to understand the wiring and identify the individual
                     components.
                     As a consequence, both representation types offer the same functionality with regard to
                     creating and editing a topology. As a consequence, you can work with one or both of these
                     display forms.
                     The topology tree or the topology graph are displayed or hidden using menu "View"
                     >"Topology tree" and "View" > "Topology graph" .
                     To display and edit several topologies, you can select these from the list of topologies
                     by making a multiple selection. The same as for "Topology comparison (Page 445)", both
                     topologies are displayed next to one another.

10.3.3             DOList Editor
                     To edit a DO list independently of CMC Expert and CMC Topo, use the "Create MyConfig
                     DOList Editor". Using the "DOList Editor", you can create and update a DO list saved centrally in
                     the company.
                     The internal DOList Editor in CMC Topo is used to create DO variables for the topology
                     currently open in CMC Topo.
                     The external DOList Editor with MCL editor is used to create a global DO variables list, e.g.
                     for a machine series, including the creation of a predefined axis-drive assignment and the
                     machine concept list. The result is used in the EPLAN add-in or in the engineering workflow
                     for automated axis-drive assignment.

                     Open "DOList Editor"
                     The "DOList Editor" is inserted in the start menu of Microsoft Windows when installing CMC.
                     If you want to create a new DO list, start the "DOList Editor" directly from the start menu of
                     Microsoft Windows.

10.3.4.3         DO list
                     To preconfigure an assignment of components to certain drives (DO), the DO in the "DO list" can
                     be extended to include components.

                     The option of permanently configuring components to certain drives (DO) is used in the
                     following scenarios:
                     1. Use in CMC Topo as basis for configuring topologies
                        A DO list can be configured and exported in CMC Topo. The DO list is saved centrally in the
                        company, for example, for a machine series.
                        Previously, you manually entered and assigned the component properties and DO properties
                        when creating new topologies. Alternatively, you can now use a DO list as basis for
                        configuring. The "*.uvdx" DO list is imported or referenced from any storage location.
                        The DOs and components configured in the DO list are offered for use when creating the
                        topology.
                        Only preconfigured drives and components are used for a referenced DO list.
                     2. Use for configuring the EPLAN with the DQ topology export
                        As described in item 1, the configured DO list in CMC Topo is used in the Siemens DQ topology
                        export (EPLAN Add-In) for deriving a topology.
                        Where the individual modules in EPLAN are assigned drives (DO) and components from the
                        DO list.
                        A description of the Siemens DQ topology export can be found in the "SINUMERIK Create
                        MyConfig - EPLAN Electric P8 Add-In (https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/ww/en/view/
                        109973917)" documentation.

Editing the component list
                      The interface of the component list is described below.

                                                                                                                        



















                                                                                                                          

①         Open DO
          Clicking the blue plus character opens a drive object (DO).
          A new dialog displays the components that belong to the DO.
②         Component display of a DO.
          The component properties are changed in the components dialog.
          Components can be added and/or deleted.
③         DO-independent components
          These components are not permanently linked with the DO.
          For example, these components are not kept when components are deleted.
④         Preconfigured components

          Preconfigured components are obtained when components are newly created below a DO.
          These components are not permanently linked with the DO and used only together with the DO.
          The preconfigured components are also automatically copied when a DO is copied.
          When a module in the topology is deleted, the preconfigured components used are not deleted.
          Preconfigured components are deleted, copied and edited via the shortcut menu in the components dialog.
⑤         Insert a new component via the drop-down list.
          Select a component class via the drop-down list. The component name is automatically created.
⑥         If the checkbox is activated, this indicates that the component is used in the topology.

Exporting a DO list
                     When exporting a "*.uvdx" DO list, all components linked with the drives (DOs) are exported,
                     irrespective of whether the components were configured via the DO list or assigned from the
                     topology to the DO.


Importing a DO list
                     When importing a "*.uvdx" DO list into an existing topology, all DO assignments are deleted.


Linked DO list
                     When linking a DO list, all existing assignments in the topology are removed. The DO assignment
                     to components is only possible when a component of the correct type, which has not been used
                     on any other component of the topology, is available for the selected DO in the DO list.
                     You can edit and add new DO and components in the linked DO list. This is possible only
                     within the DO list by clicking the button.
                     After editing, save the DO list to apply the changes.


Using a DO list when creating a new topology

                     The following variants are available for creating a new topology:




                                                                                                     
                      ① "Without preconfiguration": Opening an empty topology.
                      ② "Imported DO list": An empty topology with an imported "*.uvdx" DO list opens.
                      ③ "Linked DO list": An empty topology with a linked "*.uvdx" DO list opens.
                      ④ "Cancel": The operation is canceled.
                     Figure 10-13     Creating the topology - using the DO list

                     If one of the versions based on a DO list is selected, the DO list contains preconfigured DO
                     properties and component properties. A DO list simplifies the assignment of properties when
                     configuring the topology.

                     For new assignments of the DOs via the component properties, the preconfigured
                     components are listed for use in the DO list.

10.3.4.4         Predefinition of axis assignment for the EPLAN add-in
                     You can use the table in the "Predefinition of axis assignment" dialog to configure the required
                     assignment to the axis for each DO in the DO list.
                     The predefinition of axis assignment is only used for the import of a topology from the EPLAN
                     Add-In via the Siemens Data Exchange "*.sdx" format.
                     Whereby, the preconfiguration of the DOs used in the specific topology is performed in the
                     axis-drive assignment.
                     You can specify an axis name, the setpoint type, as well as the NC drive to be used for the
                     transport, for a selected axis.
                     In addition to the setpoint interface, you can also specify the axis to which the two encoders
                     are to be assigned. You can also configure the actual value type to be used and the NC
                     measuring system.
                     The table allows any number of DOs to be assigned to the same axis. If the topology selected
                     for the import in CMC Topo uses several DOs, for which the assignment to the same axis has
                     been configured, this assignment is rejected with a message.

10.5             Command line call


10.5.1           CMC Topo


Call
                     Write the commands shown in the following as well as the used switches and arguments in one
                     line to a batch file or a command line interface.
                     The significance of the switches and arguments is described in the following "CMC Topo
                     parameter" table.

                     Starting CMC Topo
                     CMC Topo is started with the following command, and a file can be displayed and edited.

                     Topo <Topology path>

                     Comparing topologies
                     2 topologies can be compared with the following command, i.e. 2 files are displayed and can
                     be edited.

                     Topo /diff <File1> <File2>

                     Automated CMC Topo deployment
                     For automated deployment, you can execute Create MyConfig Topo in the command line
                     mode.

                     Topo /silent <Topology path>
                           /deploy [<Deployment name>] [/deploydir <Deployment directory>]
                           /target (UST|UVDX|UTZ2) [/autocomplete]
                           [/log <Log file>] [adduvdx <Uvdx path>] [extendcompnames]

Notes

                  Note the following information for the command line call:

                  Note
                  Deployment version
                  If no deployment version is specified for the "UTZ2" deployment mode, then deployment
                  versions defined in the source for the individual CU are used. If no deployment version is
                  defined, the newest version is deployed.

                  Note
                  Observe the sequence of the switches
                  Write the switches in the specified sequence.
                  When doing this, observe the "Call" section and the "Significance of the switches" table.

                  Note
                  Path data
                  • Set the specified paths in straight quotation marks if spaces are included.
                  • Example:
                     "C:\Path with spaces\Expert_Logfile.log"
                  • Paths must never end with '\'.

                  Note
                  Saving batch files
                  Always save batch files with "ANSI/ASCII" encoding.

                                                                                              10.5 Command line call


                     Note
                     Umlauts and special characters
                     Avoid the use of umlauts and special characters in path names.
                     To allow special characters or umlauts to be correctly processed in specified paths, save the batch
                     files with command line calls with the same character set as used by the region-specific
                     command line interpreter (cmd.exe).
                     For example, Codepage "850", also known as "DOS Latin 1", applies for the region Western
                     Europe.
                     The "Notepad" editor integrated in Microsoft Windows does not support saving files with this
                     character set.

                     Note
                     Uppercase/lowercase
                     For the command line switches and arguments, always use the specified uppercase/lowercase
                     notation.

                     Note
                     Absolute/relative path
                     Either the absolute path or the relative path can be specified.
                     The relative path with ".\" or "./" refers to the current work folder, where the batch or CMD was
                     called.
                     If no path is specified, the work folder also applies.

10.6           SINAMICS device configuration


10.6.1         Production of modular machines
                  Engineering software Create MyConfig (CMC) supports both the automated production of
                  modular machines for machine manufacturers as well as the upgrade of machines for end
                  customers with only a limited number of operator actions required.
                  Producing machines with SINUMERIK ONE requires basic commissioning of the SINAMICS,
                  which is generally designated as "System configuration". You can configure the system using
                  CMC, either as "Automatic configuration" or as "User-specified topology".
                  When you configure the system in the CMC package, in the step tree you can specify all the
                  data sets and optimization data that are required within a series of modular machines in the
                  maximum machine configuration.
                  The package is adapted to the specific version of a modular machine either initially during
                  the configuring or when the package is being executed on the machine – either manually or
                  using configuration files.

10.6.2           SINAMICS device configuration with Automatic configuration or user-
                 specified topology


Applications

                     With regard to the device configuration of the SINAMICS, a general distinction is made
                     between 3 use cases that CMC supports:
                     1. SINAMICS was commissioned previously with SINUMERIK Operate or with different
                        commissioning software.
                        With a CMC package, via "Initial state" (online access) on dialog page "System configuration"
                        under "DRV archive data/drive configuration", a check of the existing drive data including the
                        topology can be carried out for the drive archive data. In addition, a further configuration or
                        optimization of the SINAMICS can be made.
                     2. The maximum configuration of the SINAMICS is wired at the machine, but the SINAMICS has
                        not yet been commissioned or configured.
                        Using a CMC package, the "Automatic configuration" under "DRV archive data/drive
                        configuration" is selected from the "System configuration" dialog page. The checks,
                        configurations or optimizations listed in item 1 in the same package are then performed.
                     3. Not all the SINAMICS components provided for the maximum configuration of the machine
                        have already been wired on the machine. For example, DQI/SMI motors are still missing.
                        SINAMICS has not yet been commissioned and configured.
                        Using a CMC package, the "User-specified topology" under "DRV archive data/drive
                        configuration" is executed from the "System configuration" dialog page. The user-specified
                        topology file is a SINAMICS offline topology package (SOT) that also contains the topology in
                        the maximum configuration of the machine. The checks, configurations or optimizations
                        listed in item 1 in the same package are then performed.


Differences between "Automatic configuration" and "User-specified topology"
                     The table below shows the major differences between "Automatic configuration" and "User-
                     specified topology." In the same way as the automatic device configuration via
                     SINUMERIK Operate, the PROFIBUS assignment (p978), the telegrams and the BICO links are also
                     entered automatically in both CMC variants.

10.6 SINAMICS device configuration


10.6.3         Drive data generation via "automatic configuration"


Basic procedure
                  The "Automatic configuration" via SINUMERIK Operate or via Create MyConfig uses the same
                  functions internally. In both cases, SINAMICS determines the "actual topology" and saves this as
                  "target topology" (p9903). This also includes the creation of drive objects (DO) and their
                  assignment in a folder structure according to bus number and slave number. Each DO is
                  represented as a PS file either in ACX or ASCII format "*.TEA". File "PS000000" is used to monitor
                  the consistency and file "PS000099" contains configuration data of the internal PROFIBUS. This
                  structure can be saved as drive archive and imported later.




                                                  '21&8

                                                  '2/LQHPRGXOHVHUYRKXEHWF




                                                  '21;
                                                  '2/LQHPRGXOHVHUYRKXEHWF



                  Figure 10-23   Drive data storage

                  For the "Automatic configuration", SINAMICS assigns the following:
                  • DO names
                  • DO numbers
                  • Component names
                  • Component numbers
                  • Component properties:
                     – Article number
                     – Component category
                     – Component type
                  The parameters for the DO are exported from the components, calculated or assigned with
                  factory settings.
                  The complete data is backed up in the drive data archive.

458                                                                             Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                                Create MyConfig - Topo
                                                                                    10.6 SINAMICS device configuration


10.6.4           Drive data generation via "user-specified topology"


Basic procedure
                     If the SINAMICS device is configured using the "user-specified topology", then the CMC package
                     specifies a SINAMICS offline_topology package for the SINAMICS in the form of a user-specified
                     topology file "*.utz2", which corresponds to the maximum machine configuration. In other
                     words, components, for example, "DQI/SMI motors", still may be missing because
                     commissioning has been performed step-by-step.
                     In addition to the topology, the user-specified topology file also specifies the following data:
                     • DO names
                     • DO numbers
                     • Component names
                     • Component numbers
                     • Component properties
                        – Article number
                        – Component type
                     The structure with generalized drive data is also specified.
                     Finally, when executed, the package requests that SINAMICS checks this data based on
                     the currently available configuration and customizes it appropriately, i.e. define the DO or
                     component status.
                     As a result SINAMICS has a customized target topology (p9903) and customized DO for the
                     specified components.
                     The DO parameters are customized by SINAMICS with the factory settings, exported from the
                     components or calculated. The complete data is backed up in the drive data archive.
                     Because at this time components not yet present in the structure have already been created,
                     you can add the associated user data to the step tree using scripts. As an alternative, for
                     example with DQI/SMI motors, export of the data from the elelconic rating plate with the
                     "motor type" or "encoder type" selection can be forced after activation.




10.6.5           Assignment of the drive data using DO variables
                     Immediately after the "Automatic configuration" or after the "User-specified topology", the
                     physical drives have been assigned to the data in the archive structure. The DOs, however, are
                     not yet assigned to the technological drive and thus to the correct NC axis.
                     If optimized drive, motor or encoder data has been configured in a CMC package for a DO, it
                     must be known to which physical DO this technological data must be assigned. This means
                     that the path address of this DO must be known. The data is assigned using DO variables.




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                          459
Create MyConfig - Topo
10.6 SINAMICS device configuration


CMC Diff
                     When configuring a package in production preparation, SINAMICS data of the modular modules
                     is extracted once as master data to ASCII files from drive archives of one or more commissioned
                     base machines with the comparison component CMC Diff (e.g. drive data, motor data, encoder
                     data of the various axes, line module data, etc.). Appropriate filter settings mean this data no
                     longer contains any topology-specific component numbers when exported.
                     When exporting, CMC Diff writes a section in front of the data, which provides a reference
                     to a topology-specific PS file in the drive data archive. This reference in the section is a short
                     form of the path, e.g. [B3_S3_PS5] instead of [BUS3.DIR\SLAVE3.DIR\PS000005.TEA].
                     These modular data sets can be maintained and managed in freely selectable folder
                     structures.


CMC Expert
                     When configuring in CMC Expert , the topology-specific path data can be replaced by symbolic,
                     topology-independent path data using a DO variable, e.g. [$(Up.doVar.psPath)]. By assigning
                     the drive-specific DO variables to a SINAMICS-DO and the associated simultaneous value
                     assignment of the DO variables using the package during runtime, the DO variable has a
                     defined value and thus also a defined path. The assignment of the DO variables to a SINAMICS-
                     DO can be done manually at runtime in a dialog or in advance during the configuration of the
                     comparison or user-specified topology. With this method, topology-independent SINAMICS
                     parameters (master data) can be flexibly and easily assigned to each DO, regardless of where the
                     drive-specific DO was placed in the SINAMICS group for the current machine.
                     As a result of the value assignment during the execution of the package, the symbolic path
                     data is replaced with absolute paths. The topology-independent SINAMICS data, which do
                     not contain any component numbers, are assigned to the drive-specific components in the
                     current topology.


Example

Execution step                                                     Result
Export of data from a drive archive in CMC Diff to an ASCII file   [B3_S3_PS5] (corresponds to the path of the data storage
with reference to the DO in the data storage.                      [BUS3.DIR\SLAVE3.DIR\PS000005.TEA])
Replacement of the reference with a symbolic path.                 [$(Up.doX.psPath)]
                                                                   […]       Section for path details in the data storage

10.6 SINAMICS device configuration



                  Note
                  We recommend that the drive data is assigned to the drive objects via the assignment of DO
                  variables. Although a direct assignment via a path specification is possible in short form, this
                  limits the flexibility and can easily result in errors.




Assignment options
                  There are 2 ways of assigning the DO variables to SINAMICS components:
                  1. When processing the package, you must manually assign the DO variables to the SINAMICS
                     components on the "SINAMICS topology" dialog page.
                  2. The DO variables are assigned to the SINAMICS components as a property during the
                     configuration of a comparison topology or user-specified topology.
                     The two topologies are linked into the project on the "SINAMICS topology" dialog page. Which
                     topology is used during the runtime depends on the configuration of the DRV area on the
                     "System configuration" dialog page.




10.6.6         The advantages of using comparison or user-specified topology
                  The configuration of a comparison or user-specified topology with CMC Topo and the use of the
                  file in the package, offer a number of additional advantages.


Advantages for the configuration of the topology with CMC Topo
                  • Understandable topology creation thanks to a graphical wiring diagram
                  • Support with component box, shortcut menu, check run and graphic / color-coded
                    visualization
                  • Printing the wiring diagram of the SINAMICS components with legend for documentation
                    purposes
                  • Comparison of topologies
                  • Import of topologies from drive archives
                  • Management of DO variables


Advantages of the topology file during the package execution
                  • The actual wiring of the SINAMICS in the control cabinet can be checked based on the
                    machine topology exported from SINAMICS. Warning or error messages are issued should
                    deviations occur.
                  • You can check the properties of the components wired via DRIVE-CLiQ (DO type, article
                    number, etc.). Wildcards are allowed when specifying the article number, e.g. "1FK7042
                    xAF7x xFxx".



                                                                                      Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
462                                                                        Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL
                                                                                              Create MyConfig - Topo
                                                                                 10.6 SINAMICS device configuration


                     • Sensor Modules not directly wired to a Motor Module, but rather to a hub or a CU, can be
                       uniquely assigned to a DO.
                     • The specification of an OEM ID is used to assign the SINAMICS-CU local component number
                       to a particular OEM global unique identifier. During package execution, the OEM component
                       number in DO1 is written to parameter "p7859" [Component number].
                     • For the comparison topology, the DO names, DO numbers and component names specified
                       by SINAMICS for the " Automatic configuration" can be replaced by user-specific data.
                       DO names
                       If a DO name change has been configured, then it is automatically entered in SINAMICS
                       parameter "p199".
                       DO number
                       When the drive device is being configured, SINAMICS assigns the DO numbers for all DO at
                       the "CU" and the "NX", i.e. locally for the CU, starting with number "1".
                       For a machine series, it is more transparent, for example, if the X drive, irrespective of its
                       positioning in the SINAMICS group, always has the same number. And that the DO numbers
                       in the SINAMICS group are unique, and do not occur several times.
                       The value range for the DO numbers lies between "2" and "54".
                       Component names
                       You can freely assign component names. The names of the SINAMICS components are
                       displayed on the dialogs and in the screen forms and messages of SINUMERIK Operate.
                     • When a user-specified topology is used, the component numbers must also be specified in
                       addition to the DO names, DO numbers and component names.
                       The use of the DO names, DO numbers and component names corresponds to the above
                       explanations for the comparison topology.
                       You must also specify the component numbers for the user-specified topology. "CU" and "NX"
                       must be assigned the "1"; it is not permissible that the numbers are assigned twice on the "CU"
                       or "NX".
                       The value range for the component numbers lies in the range between "2" and "199".
                       In CMC Topo, you can also automatically assign the component numbers via the shortcut
                       menu.
                     • When configuring a user-specified topology, you can specify the activation status of the DO
                       and components.
                       The following applies:
                        – 0     inactive and available
                        – 1     active and available
                        – 2     not available
                        The status is entered in the following parameters:
                        – p105 DO activation/deactivation
                        – p125 Motor Module activation/deactivation
                        – p145 Sensor Module activation/deactivation

10.6.7             Configuration of the topology with CMC Topo
                      Using Create MyConfig Topo, you can configure a user-specified topology or a comparison
                      topology. Using Create MyConfig Topo is described in Section CMC Topo - Operation (Page 422).
                      The wiring diagram for the DRIVE-CLiQ connections and some of the properties are identical
                      for all topologies.
                      With switchover from comparison topology to user-specified topology, the additional
                      properties DO activation, component activation and component number must also be
                      specified.
                      When switching over to comparison topology, the data remains stored to be able to switch
                      back to user-specified topology. This data has no effect in the comparison topology.
                      For the deployment as user-specified topology, other necessary data is added internally and
                      output as binary user-specified topology file.
                      To deploy a user-specified topology, it is necessary to specify a CNC software version.

10.6.8           Generation of the comparison topology using external software
                     The structure and the contents of the comparison topology for a package is an open and
                     documented interface, the CMC Topo-XML interface. The file format is XML.
                     The CMC Topo-XML interface allows the comparison topology to also be generated using
                     external software, which is integrated in the PLM process of the machine builder, e.g.
                     EPLAN or ELCAD. The externally generated comparison topologies can also be imported into
                     CMC Topo and changed in production planning for checking purposes or modifications before
                     they are integrated into the project when configuring with CMC Expert.
                     On the dialog side "SINAMICS topology", during the runtime, you can also manually select a
                     comparison configuration file, which lies in or next to the package.
                     Generally, you create a special topology for each machine variant, while one package can be
                     sufficient for all machines.

11.1             Restoring the initial state of a USB flash drive
                     To be able to use a USB flash drive for CMC, you must make sure that the partitions are created
                     correctly.
                     A USB flash drive can be used without problems on a PC, whereas it cannot be used to run
                     a CMC package on an NCU/PPU. This may be due to the partitions or the file system on the
                     USB flash drive.


Requirement
                     To format a USB flash drive, observe the following notes:
                     • No special program is required on a PC with Microsoft Windows.
                     • You need administrator rights.


Formatting a USB flash drive
                     Carry out the following instructions if your USB flash drive does not start with a CMC package on
                     an NCU/PPU or if similar problems arise:

                      diskpart
                      list disk
                      sel disk <n>
                      clean
                      create part primary
                      format quick fs=fat32 label="CMC"
                     On a PC with Microsoft Windows, you enter the instructions at the command prompt. On
                     Linux PCs, you use other options such as "gparted".


Procedure
                     1. In Microsoft Windows, open the command line and type diskpart.
                        The utility for partitioning hard disks and removable data storage media is started in a new
                        window. If a UAC prompt appears in Microsoft Windows, confirm with "Yes".
                     2. The data storage media detected are displayed after you enter list disk. Based on the
                        memory size of the USB flash drive, determine the number of the data storage medium. In
                        this example, it is data storage medium 1.




Create MyConfig - Diff, Expert, Topo
Operating Manual, 06/2026, A5E50115644B AL                                                                        467
FAQs
11.2 Important folders and files


                   3. Sel disk 1 selects this data storage medium. Use the correct number based on the
                      available data storage medium.

                       NOTICE
                       Select Sel disk
                       If an incorrect number is specified, an unwanted data storage medium may be destroyed.

                   4. clean erases the data storage medium chosen via the number. All data on it is erased!
                   5. create part primary creates a primary partition on the data storage medium.
                   6. format quick fs=fat32 label="CMC" runs fast formatting with fat32. The USB flash
                      drive is assigned the name "CMC".

                                                                  11.3 Simulating a project based on offline archives


11.3             Simulating a project based on offline archives

Requirement
                     A package that has been configured for the use of an NCU or PCU, is simulated under certain
                     constraints without the real existing NCU or PCU.


Constraints
                     Take the following constraints into account:
                     • All configurations that refer to a non-existing NCU are not processed by the package during
                       simulation.
                        Note
                        The NCU is not simulated.

                     • If archives are available, the configurations relevant for archive data are executed.
                     • The "System configuration" dialog is only available when a real NCU is used, not with the
                       deactivated data area of the "NCU/PPU".
                     • An automatic configuration of the drives or a user-specified topology is not simulated directly.
                       However, if you use an appropriate drive archive as initial offline archive, you can simulate the
                       "SINAMICS topology" dialog in the "Comparison topology" version.
                     • Control versions of the NCU are not evaluated and not simulated.


Procedure
                     To simulate a package without using a real NCU/PCU or PCU, in CMC Expert in the "Project
                     explorer", use the subsequently described settings.

                     Configuration
                     • In "Configuration", set the properties group "Package creation" > "Runtime system" >
                       "Windows package (PC/IPC)".
                       A package is always only simulated under Microsoft Windows.
                     • Since the NCU/PPU is not really available, select "No" for "Use NCU/PPU" under "Data areas".
                       All package parts that are relevant for the NCU are therefore ignored for the package
                       execution.
                       The NCU is not simulated.

                     Dialog pages
                     • Store the archives that serve as basis for all archive data manipulations in the "Select offline
                       archive" dialog.
                       Use a "NPDHSL" archive of your control, e.g. "Backup_NPDHSL_2019-10-25.dsf", in parts or
                       as a whole, from the initial state before the package is executed.

11.4           First encoder of a drive on the CU or downstream of the HUB

Automatic configuration not possible
                  If during a drive data generation via "Automatic configuration" a first encoder (SMI or SMC) is
                  connected downstream of a HUB or to the CU, then a complete automatic configuration of the
                  drive by SINAMICS and CMC Shield is not possible.
                  Parameter "P1982" (Pole position identification on) is set to "1" by SINAMICS instead of "0"
                  and is not corrected automatically.


Remedy
                  The user can correct the parameter manually or in the step tree of a CMC package.
                  Set parameter "P1982=0" in the step tree in a component for all drives whose first encoder is
                  connected downstream of the HUB or to the CU.




11.5           Parallel connection of Active Line Modules (ALM)

Requirement
                  The following versions are required:
                  • Create MyConfig from V6.2
                  • SINUMERIK ONE from V6.14
                  • SINAMICS from V5.20


Active Line Module
                  As of SINAMICS 5.20 you can connect 2 Active Line Modules (ALM) to a CU or NX. The Active Line
                  Modules are operated in parallel connection. The parameters of both ALM are saved in one drive
                  object (DO).
                  The required function module is created automatically in all commissioning variants. This
                  function is only possible with components greater than 55 kW. The deployed components
                  must have the same power parameters.

11.6             SINAMICS Starter: No access to drive after CMC package

After the CMC package has been executed, SINAMICS Starter cannot access the drive
                     When configuring components that are not ordinarily available ("p105 == 0" or "p125 == 2"),
                     problems can be incurred when SINAMICS Starter attempts to access the drive device.


Remedy
                     The problem exists until the component is installed for the first time. A subsequent problem
                     involving SINAMICS Starter can be circumvented by deleting the Article No.




11.7             Certain package names result in an error message in Microsoft
                 Windows

Avoiding the error message "This program might not have installed correctly"
                     Windows packages that have the designations "install", "installation" or "setup" in their names
                     result in a confirmation prompt from Microsoft Windows when starting the package on a PCU.
                     Moreover, Microsoft Windows usually reports that the program has not been installed properly.

                   • At least 1 uppercase letter
                   • At least 1 lowercase letter
                   • At least 1 number




11.9           Absolute and relative paths
                   Generally, path data are managed in relative terms in CMC Expert. The precondition is that the
                   link points to the same drive on which the project is located.
                   Links, which point to another drive, are always saved with absolute path data.


Relative paths
                   • Linked script libraries (from CMC V6.8 SP1)
                   • Files in dialogs (from CMC V6.8 SP1)
                      – Package configurations
                      – tgz files
                      – Archives in dialogs
                      – ust, utz2, mcl files
                   • Linked actions and scripts in the step tree
                   • Linked files in actions (paths are relative to the action)


Absolute paths
                  • Linked steps (even if the link points to the same drive)
                  • Links, which point to another drive

                                                                           11.10 Determining the encoding of a script


11.10            Determining the encoding of a script
                     When saving scripts and files in actions, you can select between UTF-8 and ISO 8859-1 (Latin-1)
                     encoding.
                     When creating a new file, the default setting is UTF-8. This applies to both scripts as well as to
                     tasks and files in actions.
                     When opening an existing file, the file is checked and the actual encoding determined. The
                     determined encoding is displayed in the selection box.
                     • A check is first made as to whether the file contains special characters (characters not
                       belonging to the ASCII character set, e.g. umlauts or special letters like ß, ñ, ...).
                       If the file does not contain any special characters, then UTF-8 is assumed as default value for
                       further editing. If a special character is added, it is saved with UTF-8 encoding accordingly.
                     • If the file contains a special character and is UTF-8 encoded, then UTF-8 is recognized.
                     • If the file contains a special character and is recognized to be encoded in Latin-1 (file is not in
                       conformance with UTF-8 and Latin-1 is recognizable), then Latin-1 is recognized.
                     • If neither of the 2 encodings are recognized:
                        – For scripts, Latin-1 is assumed as the fallback level. When doing this it is assumed that the
                          file was also previously edited using CMC Expert and for scripts, CMC Expert previously
                          only recognized Latin-1 encoding.
                        – For tasks and files in actions, UTF-8 is assumed as the fallback level.
                     • Although changing the default setting for encoding influences the way in which the file is
                       saved, it does not influence the current interpretation. The file is not read-in again.
                     • UTF-8 files are saved without BOM (Byte Order Mark), unless the file already contains a BOM.
                       An existing BOM is kept.
